Mercy usually costs something. Time, money, pride, the right to be right. That is what makes it mercy and not just being nice. Jesus was merciful all the way to a cross.

We find it easy to want mercy for ourselves and justice for everyone else. This verse flips that. Be the one who gives the grace you hope to receive.

Is there someone you have been holding a debt against? Today might be the day to let it go.

beatitudes.title: Lock in the fifth line
beatitudes.practice: Say Matthew 5:3-7 from memory while doing a chore. Push the hide game up a level.
beatitudes.body:
Five down. Look how far you have come. Poor in spirit, mourn, meek, hunger and thirst, merciful. You are carrying more than half of the Beatitudes in your heart now.

A good test today. Say them while you are doing something else, folding laundry, walking, driving. If you can say them with your hands busy, they are becoming part of you, not just something you recite.

beatitudes.title: The pure in heart
beatitudes.practice: Add Matthew 5:8. Say verses 3 through 8 in order.
beatitudes.body:
Line six: Blessed are the pure in heart, for they will see God.

Pure in heart means undivided. It is a heart that is not split between God and a hundred other loyalties. Not perfect, but honest. No hidden rooms, no secret self. What you see is what is really there.

And the promise is the greatest one yet. They will see God. Purity is not about being good enough to earn a look at Him. It is that a clean window lets the light through. When our hearts are undivided, we finally see Him clearly.

beatitudes.title: An undivided heart
beatitudes.practice: Say verses 3 through 8 from memory. Sit quiet for one minute and ask God to make your heart undivided.
beatitudes.body:
A divided heart is exhausting. Trying to serve God and also protect an image, chase approval, and keep a secret all at once will wear you out. Jesus offers something simpler. One heart, pointed one way.

Purity of heart is not about never messing up. It is about not hiding when you do. It is bringing the whole self into the light, even the parts you are ashamed of. That is where you see God most clearly, in the honesty.

Is there a corner of your heart you have kept in the dark? He is gentle. Bring it to Him.

beatitudes.title: Lock in the sixth line
beatitudes.practice: Say Matthew 5:3-8 from memory. Teach one verse to someone younger than you.
beatitudes.body:
Six down. Only two more Beatitudes to learn. You are so close to having the whole list.

Here is a fun one for today. If you have kids around, teach them verse 8. Kids memorize fast, and teaching someone else is the best way to cement it in your own mind. Make it a little game at dinner.

beatitudes.title: The peacemakers
beatitudes.practice: Add Matthew 5:9. Say verses 3 through 9 in order.
beatitudes.body:
Line seven: Blessed are the peacemakers, for they will be called children of God.

Notice it says peacemakers, not peacekeepers. Keeping the peace often means avoiding, staying quiet, letting things slide. Making peace is active. It steps into the mess and works to reconcile. It costs something.

And look at the reward. They will be called children of God. When you make peace, you look like your Father, because that is exactly what He did for us through Jesus. Peacemaking is the family resemblance.

beatitudes.title: Make peace, do not just keep it
beatitudes.practice: Say verses 3 through 9 from memory. Take one step toward peace with someone today.
beatitudes.body:
Peacemaking is hard because it usually means going first. Being the one to apologize, to reach out, to break the silence. It is easier to keep score. But Jesus blesses the ones who lay down the scorecard and build a bridge.

This does not mean pretending everything is fine. Real peace deals with the real thing. It is honest and kind at the same time.

Is there a relationship where you could go first this week?

beatitudes.title: Lock in the seventh line
beatitudes.practice: Say Matthew 5:3-9 from memory twice. Spend extra time on any line that trips you up.
beatitudes.body:
Seven down. One Beatitude left. You can almost say the whole thing.

You are at the level now where the hide game should be covering half the words and you can still fill them in. If that feels hard, that is normal. Keep going back to the ones that trip you up. Those sticky spots just need a few more reps.

beatitudes.title: The persecuted
beatitudes.practice: Add Matthew 5:10. You now have all eight. Say verses 3 through 10 in order.
beatitudes.body:
The eighth and final line: Blessed are those who are persecuted because of righteousness, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.

This is the hard one. Jesus is honest that doing the right thing sometimes costs you. People may misunderstand you, push back, even turn on you. He does not promise the Christian life will be easy. He promises it will be worth it.

And look, the list ends where it began. Theirs is the kingdom of heaven. The very same reward as the poor in spirit. The circle closes. Blessing at the start, blessing at the end.

beatitudes.title: Blessed when it costs you
beatitudes.practice: Say verses 3 through 10 from memory. That is all eight Beatitudes. Sit with that for a second.
beatitudes.body:
Most of us will not face real persecution. But we all know the smaller version, being left out, laughed at, or judged for doing what is right. Jesus sees it, and He calls it blessed.

The reward is not someday only. It is theirs, present tense, the kingdom of heaven belongs to them right now. When standing for what is right costs you, you are not losing. You are in good company, and the kingdom is yours.

Have you ever paid a price for doing the right thing? Jesus saw it.

beatitudes.title: Lock in all eight
beatitudes.practice: Say Matthew 5:3-10 from memory three times. Smooth out the rough spots.
beatitudes.body:
You did it. All eight Beatitudes are in your heart. Today is not about learning a new line, it is about running the whole list until it flows.

Say them start to finish. Then again. Then again. Each time it gets a little smoother. The goal is not just to recall them but to be able to say them like you mean them, because you do.

Tomorrow we add the last piece Jesus said, the part where He turns and speaks straight to you.

beatitudes.title: When they say all kinds of evil
beatitudes.practice: Add Matthew 5:11-12. Say the entire passage, verses 3 through 12, from memory.
beatitudes.body:
After the eight, Jesus turns personal. He stops saying blessed are they and starts saying blessed are you. Verses 11 and 12: Blessed are you when people insult you, persecute you and falsely say all kinds of evil against you because of me. Rejoice and be glad, because great is your reward in heaven.

This is Jesus looking right at you. When it comes, and it may, His instruction is almost shocking. Rejoice. Be glad. Not because the pain is not real, but because you are in the long line of prophets who stood for God and the reward is huge.

Add these two verses to your recitation. Now you have the whole passage.

beatitudes.title: Put it all together
beatitudes.practice: Say Matthew 5:3-12 from memory. Try making up a simple tune for it, or walking while you say it.
beatitudes.body:
You have every piece now. Today we make it one smooth thing instead of nine separate parts.

Here is a tip. Say it with your body. Some people walk while they recite. Some tap the rhythm. Some have made up a simple tune and sing it, and honestly that is the fastest way of all. If a song helps you, make one up and do not overthink it. Nobody has to hear it but you and God.

Run the whole passage a few times today. You are almost there.

beatitudes.title: Say it without looking
beatitudes.practice: Play the hide game at the hardest level you can. Say the whole passage out loud twice.
beatitudes.body:
Today, close the book and say the whole thing. When you hit a wall, do not peek right away. Sit in it for a second and let your memory reach for it. That reaching is what makes it permanent.

Most of the words are hidden in the practice game now. If you can fill in eighty percent from memory, you are ready for the home stretch.

You have carried this passage for almost a month. It is becoming part of who you are.

beatitudes.title: Almost there
beatitudes.practice: Recite Matthew 5:3-12 to one other person, out loud, from memory.
beatitudes.body:
One day before the finish. Today, say the entire passage to another person. Your spouse, your kid, a friend, whoever. Saying it out loud to a real face is different than saying it alone, and it will show you how solid it really is.

Do not worry about being perfect. Worry about meaning it. These are not just words you memorized. This is the heart of Jesus, and it is in you now.

Tomorrow is the celebration, and your challenge to share it.

beatitudes.title: You hid it in your heart
beatitudes.practice: Record yourself saying Matthew 5:3-12 from memory. Share it with #HideItInYourHeart, then open your certificate.
beatitudes.body:
Thirty days ago these were words on a page. Today they live in you. That is a real thing, and it does not go away. You have hidden the Beatitudes in your heart, and no one can take them.

Here is the final challenge, and it is a fun one. Record yourself saying the whole passage from memory. Just your phone, no need to be polished. Then share it. Post it on your dashboard here, and put it on Facebook or Instagram with the hashtag HideItInYourHeart. Your recording might be the nudge that gets someone else to start.

Then grab your certificate. You earned every word of it. I am so proud of you.

proverbs.subject: Day 1: Where wisdom starts
proverbs.title: Wisdom begins with taking God seriously.
proverbs.focus: Everyone shares one thing they want to get wiser about this month.
proverbs.prayer_focus:
What is something you know a lot about? Who taught you?
What do you think it means to take God seriously?
proverbs.prayer_verse:
What is the difference between being smart and being wise?
Verse 7 says fools despise wisdom. Why do you think people ignore good advice even when they know it is good?
proverbs.practice: No table needed. The car works great: read the verses at pickup or on the way to practice and talk on the drive.
proverbs.body:
Proverbs opens by telling us why it exists: to make us wise. And then it hands us the key in verse 7. The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge. That does not mean being scared of God. It means taking Him seriously, the way you take gravity seriously.

Everything else this month builds on that one idea. Wise people start with God.

proverbs.subject: Day 2: Digging for treasure
proverbs.title: Wisdom goes to the people who search for it.
proverbs.focus: Hide something small in the house or car and let the kids hunt for it. Then talk about verse 4: search for wisdom like that.
proverbs.prayer_focus:
If you could dig up any treasure, what would you want to find?
Where do you think a person digs to find wisdom?
proverbs.prayer_verse:
What is something valuable that took you real effort to get? Was it worth it?
What would searching for wisdom actually look like in your week?
proverbs.practice: Let a kid read the verses out loud. Kids remember what they read to the family far better than what they are read.
proverbs.body:
Chapter 2 says to look for wisdom like silver, to search for it like hidden treasure. Treasure does not fall on you. You dig.

God is not hiding wisdom from us. He promises to give it to anyone who honestly looks. But looking is the part we skip.

proverbs.subject: Day 3: Trust with your whole heart
proverbs.title: Trust God with all your heart, not just the easy parts.
proverbs.focus: Have everyone memorize Proverbs 3:5 together tonight. Race to say it fastest.
proverbs.prayer_focus:
Who do you trust to catch you if you fell? Why them?
What is something you trust God to take care of?
proverbs.prayer_verse:
What is one area where you would rather trust your own plan than ask God? Be honest.
What makes trusting God hard when you cannot see how something ends?
proverbs.practice: Play the chapter on the Bible app while everyone eats or rides. Audio counts.
proverbs.body:
Proverbs 3:5-6 might be the most famous verses in the book. Trust in the LORD with all your heart and lean not on your own understanding.

Everyone trusts something: their plan, their feelings, their own smarts. Proverbs says trust the One who sees the whole road, and He will keep your paths straight.

proverbs.subject: Day 4: Guard your heart
proverbs.title: What you let into your heart runs your whole life.
proverbs.focus: As a family, name one thing you will let in more of this month, and one thing you will guard against.
proverbs.prayer_focus:
What kinds of things do we lock up or protect? Why?
What is something good you want to keep in your heart?
proverbs.prayer_verse:
What actually gets into your heart most each day, and does it make you better or worse?
If everything you do flows from your heart, what does your week say is in there?
proverbs.practice: Breakfast works as well as dinner. Attach it to a meal you already share.
proverbs.body:
Chapter 4 gives one of the biggest commands in the book: above all else, guard your heart, for everything you do flows from it.

We lock the front door but leave our hearts wide open to whatever wants in. What you watch, hear, and dwell on becomes what you do.

proverbs.subject: Day 5: Keeping promises
proverbs.title: Faithful people keep their promises even when it costs them.
proverbs.focus: Each person makes one small, real promise to the family for this week. Write them down. Check back Friday.
proverbs.prayer_focus:
What is a promise someone kept to you? How did it feel?
Why is it hard to keep a promise sometimes?
proverbs.prayer_verse:
Have you ever had someone break a promise to you? What did it change?
What is one commitment you want to be known for keeping?
proverbs.practice: With little ones, one or two verses is plenty. You do not need the whole chapter to have the conversation.
proverbs.body:
Chapter 5 is about faithfulness, staying true to the people you have committed to. It is written to grown-ups about marriage, but the root is for everyone: promises matter.

God sees everything we do, verse 21 says. Faithfulness is who you are when no one is checking.

proverbs.subject: Day 6: Watch the ant
proverbs.title: Nobody has to make the ant work. Be like the ant.
proverbs.focus: Tonight everyone does one chore nobody asked them to do. Compare notes tomorrow.
proverbs.prayer_focus:
What do ants do all day? What would happen if they all stopped?
What is one job you can do without being asked?
proverbs.prayer_verse:
What is the thing you put off the most, and what does it cost you?
What is the difference between resting and being lazy?
proverbs.practice: Let the kids ask the questions tonight. Hand a young reader the questions and let them run it.
proverbs.body:
Proverbs 6 says: go watch the ants. Nobody supervises them. Nobody nags them. They just see the work and do it.

Laziness never announces itself. It whispers a little more sleep, a little more scrolling. Proverbs says the wise see what needs doing and start.

proverbs.subject: Day 7: Avoiding traps
proverbs.title: Wisdom sees the trap before you step in it.
proverbs.focus: Make a family code word anyone can text or say when they feel stuck in a bad situation and need a way out, no questions asked.
proverbs.prayer_focus:
How does a mouse trap work? Why does the mouse go to it?
What is something that looks fun but can hurt you?
proverbs.prayer_verse:
What is a real trap for people your age that looks harmless at first?
How do you actually get out of a tempting situation? What is your move?
proverbs.practice: Older kid not home? Text them the teen question and let them answer by text. It still counts.
proverbs.body:
Chapter 7 tells a story of someone walking straight into a trap because it looked good at first. The whole chapter is a warning: temptation never looks like a trap at the start.

Wisdom is looking down the road. Not just is this fun now, but where does this path end?

proverbs.subject: Day 8: Wisdom is shouting
proverbs.title: God's wisdom is not hidden. It is calling out to anyone who will listen.
proverbs.focus: Everyone names one person they will actually ask for advice this month, and what they will ask.
proverbs.prayer_focus:
If wisdom had a voice, what do you think it would sound like?
Who in your life gives you really good advice?
proverbs.prayer_verse:
When was the last time you knew the right thing and did the opposite? What drowned out the voice?
Verse 11 says wisdom is worth more than rubies. Do you actually believe that? What do people our age treat as more valuable?
proverbs.practice: Missed a day or three? No guilt. Just do today's. The goal is talking about wisdom as a family, not a perfect streak.
proverbs.body:
In chapter 8, wisdom stands at the crossroads and shouts. She is not whispering in a secret club. She is in the street, calling everyone.

Most of the time we do not lack wisdom. We lack the listening. The voice is there: parents, Scripture, wise friends, that nudge in your gut you keep overriding.

proverbs.subject: Day 9: Two invitations
proverbs.title: Every day, wisdom and foolishness both invite you to dinner.
proverbs.focus: At dinner or in the car, list three choices tomorrow will bring and decide the wise RSVP for each, out loud, in advance.
proverbs.prayer_focus:
If two friends invited you over at the same time, how would you pick?
What is one wise choice you made this week?
proverbs.prayer_verse:
What does Folly's invitation look like for you specifically? It is different for everyone.
Verse 8 says wise people love correction. How do you react when someone corrects you?
proverbs.practice: No table needed. The car works great: read the verses at pickup or on the way to practice and talk on the drive.
proverbs.body:
Chapter 9 pictures two houses. Wisdom builds hers and sets a table. Folly sits at her door and calls out too. Same street, two invitations, every single day.

You cannot accept both. Every choice is an RSVP.

proverbs.subject: Day 10: Words that build, words that break
proverbs.title: Your mouth is either a fountain of life or a wrecking ball.
proverbs.focus: Fountain night: everyone says one true, kind sentence about each person present. No repeats, no jokes.
proverbs.prayer_focus:
What is the nicest thing someone said to you this week?
How do you feel when someone uses mean words at you?
proverbs.prayer_verse:
Is your default with your siblings building or tearing? What would they say?
Verse 19 says fewer words means fewer sins. When should you have just stayed quiet recently?
proverbs.practice: Let a kid read the verses out loud. Kids remember what they read to the family far better than what they are read.
proverbs.body:
Chapter 10 begins the one-liners, and a bunch of them are about the mouth. The mouth of the righteous is a fountain of life, verse 11 says. And verse 19: when words are many, sin is not absent.

Every family has a word culture. Today is a good day to look at ours.

proverbs.subject: Day 11: Honest scales
proverbs.title: God loves honesty in the small stuff nobody sees.
proverbs.focus: Truth check: each person shares one small thing they were not fully honest about lately. No punishments tonight, just clean slates.
proverbs.prayer_focus:
Why is it wrong to cheat in a game, even a little?
Have you ever told the truth when it was hard? What happened?
proverbs.prayer_verse:
What is a small dishonesty people your age think does not count?
Verse 3 says integrity guides you. How does being known as honest actually make life easier?
proverbs.practice: Play the chapter on the Bible app while everyone eats or rides. Audio counts.
proverbs.body:
Chapter 11 opens with dishonest scales, a merchant quietly cheating customers a little at a time. The LORD detests it. He delights in accuracy.

Most dishonesty is small. The half-answer to a parent. Rounding up your effort. God cares about the small honest thing because that is where character is built.

proverbs.subject: Day 12: Who you listen to
proverbs.title: Wise people love being corrected. Fools hate it.
proverbs.focus: Parents go first tonight: share a correction you received as an adult and how it helped you. Then invite the kids to share one.
proverbs.prayer_focus:
When mom or dad corrects you, what is it for?
Can you remember a rule that kept you safe?
proverbs.prayer_verse:
What is your honest first reaction to correction: listen, argue, or shut down?
Who is allowed to correct you? If the answer is nobody, what does that say?
proverbs.practice: Breakfast works as well as dinner. Attach it to a meal you already share.
proverbs.body:
Verse 1 of chapter 12 is blunt: whoever loves discipline loves knowledge, but whoever hates correction is stupid. Proverbs does not soften it.

Correction is a gift wrapped in something uncomfortable. The wise open it anyway.

proverbs.subject: Day 13: Choose your walking partners
proverbs.title: Walk with the wise and you get wiser. Walk with fools and you get hurt.
proverbs.focus: Everyone names one wise person they want more time with, and the family figures out how to make one of those happen this month.
proverbs.prayer_focus:
Who are your best friends? What do you like doing together?
How do friends change how we act?
proverbs.prayer_verse:
Think about your closest three friends. Are they making you wiser or pulling you down?
What kind of walking partner are YOU for your friends?
proverbs.practice: With little ones, one or two verses is plenty. You do not need the whole chapter to have the conversation.
proverbs.body:
Proverbs 13:20 is one to memorize as a family: walk with the wise and become wise, for a companion of fools suffers harm.

You become like the people you spend time with. Not instantly. Gradually, like walking a trail together.

proverbs.subject: Day 14: Building your house
proverbs.title: Every day you are either building your home or tearing it down.
proverbs.focus: Build something together tonight or this weekend: blocks with littles, a puzzle, pancakes. While you build, talk about what builds a family.
proverbs.prayer_focus:
What do you need to build a strong house?
What is one thing that makes our family strong?
proverbs.prayer_verse:
What do you personally add to this family when you are at your best?
What is one habit of yours that tears at the house? You do not have to say it out loud, but name it to yourself.
proverbs.practice: Let the kids ask the questions tonight. Hand a young reader the questions and let them run it.
proverbs.body:
Chapter 14 starts with a picture: the wise woman builds her house, but the foolish one tears hers down with her own hands. That is true of everyone in a family, not just moms.

Every kindness is a brick laid. Every eye-roll, slammed door, and cutting remark pulls one out. Houses go up slowly and come down fast.

proverbs.subject: Day 15: The gentle answer
proverbs.title: A gentle answer turns away anger. A harsh word stirs it up.
proverbs.focus: Practice round: act out someone taking your seat, and respond two ways, harsh then gentle. Laugh about it. Then use the gentle one for real this week.
proverbs.prayer_focus:
Show me your gentle voice. Now show me your grumpy voice. Which one makes people listen?
What can you do when someone is angry at you?
proverbs.prayer_verse:
Think of your last blow-up with someone in this house. Where was the moment it could have gone differently?
Why does going gentle feel like losing? Is it?
proverbs.practice: Older kid not home? Text them the teen question and let them answer by text. It still counts.
proverbs.body:
Proverbs 15:1 might be the most practical verse in the whole book for a household. A gentle answer turns away wrath, but a harsh word stirs up anger.

Every argument has a moment where it could go either way. One person going gentle, on purpose, changes the whole room.

proverbs.subject: Day 16: Who directs your steps
proverbs.title: You can make your plans, but God directs your steps.
proverbs.focus: Everyone shares one plan they have, then prays one sentence: God, direct my steps.
proverbs.prayer_focus:
What do you want to be when you grow up?
Has a day ever turned out different than you thought, but better?
proverbs.prayer_verse:
What is your current plan for your life? How would you handle God redirecting it?
Verse 18 warns pride comes before a fall. Where does pride sneak into your plans?
proverbs.practice: Missed a day or three? No guilt. Just do today's. The goal is talking about wisdom as a family, not a perfect streak.
proverbs.body:
Proverbs 16:9 says we make our plans, but the LORD establishes our steps. Plans are good. Proverbs is not against planning. It is against planning like you are God.

Hold your plans with an open hand. Some of the best things in your life will be interruptions.

proverbs.subject: Day 17: A friend at all times
proverbs.title: Real friends love you on your worst day, and a cheerful heart is good medicine.
proverbs.focus: Medicine night: watch or tell the funniest family story you have. Someone will say I remember when, and let it roll from there.
proverbs.prayer_focus:
Who came to help you last time you were sad or hurt?
What makes our whole family laugh?
proverbs.prayer_verse:
Are you an all-times friend, or a good-times friend?
Who in your life needs a brother or sister born for adversity right now?
proverbs.practice: No table needed. The car works great: read the verses at pickup or on the way to practice and talk on the drive.
proverbs.body:
Two gems today. Verse 17: a friend loves at all times, and a brother is born for adversity. Verse 22: a cheerful heart is good medicine.

Family is who shows up on the hard days. And laughter in a house is not extra, it is medicine.

proverbs.subject: Day 18: Listen before you answer
proverbs.title: Answering before you listen is folly and shame.
proverbs.focus: The echo game at dinner or in the car: before you can answer anyone, repeat their point back in your own words first. Try it for ten minutes.
proverbs.prayer_focus:
How can you tell when someone is really listening to you?
What are good listening ears like?
proverbs.prayer_verse:
Who actually listens all the way to the end of your sentences? How does it feel?
In your last argument, could you repeat back what the other person actually said?
proverbs.practice: Let a kid read the verses out loud. Kids remember what they read to the family far better than what they are read.
proverbs.body:
Proverbs 18:13: to answer before listening, that is folly and shame. We all do it. We are loading our reply while the other person is still talking.

Listening is love with its mouth closed. It is also how the wise learn anything.

proverbs.subject: Day 19: Patience and the long way
proverbs.title: A patient person has great understanding. Hot tempers make everything worse.
proverbs.focus: Pick the family flashpoint (getting out the door, bedtime, chores) and agree on one patient move everyone will try there this week.
proverbs.prayer_focus:
What is the hardest thing to wait for?
What happens when someone loses their temper over something little?
proverbs.prayer_verse:
What is the last offense you could have overlooked but did not? Was the fight worth it?
Where does impatience cost you most: family, friends, school?
proverbs.practice: Play the chapter on the Bible app while everyone eats or rides. Audio counts.
proverbs.body:
Chapter 19 keeps circling patience. Verse 11: a person's wisdom yields patience; it is to one's glory to overlook an offense.

Overlooking an offense does not mean pretending. It means you are strong enough not to need every fight.

proverbs.subject: Day 20: Known by your actions
proverbs.title: Even a child is known by their actions.
proverbs.focus: Each person picks one word they want to be known for this year. Write them on a card and stick it on the fridge or the dashboard.
proverbs.prayer_focus:
What do you want your teacher to say about you?
What is one good thing you did today?
proverbs.prayer_verse:
What are you currently known for? Is it what you want to be known for?
One action this week could start changing your reputation where it needs it. What is it?
proverbs.practice: Breakfast works as well as dinner. Attach it to a meal you already share.
proverbs.body:
Proverbs 20:11 says even small children are known by whether their conduct is pure and right. What you do is your reputation, at any age.

Everyone in the family already has a track record: with teachers, coaches, friends, each other. The good news is a track record is built one action at a time, starting today.

proverbs.subject: Day 21: Doing right beats looking right
proverbs.title: God cares more about doing what is right than looking religious.
proverbs.focus: Secret mission: everyone does one right and just thing for somebody outside the family this week without telling them. Report back Sunday.
proverbs.prayer_focus:
What is the difference between doing a chore and just saying you did?
What is something right you can do for someone tomorrow?
proverbs.prayer_verse:
Where is it tempting to look good instead of be good, at church, online, at school?
What would change if God graded your week by verse 3?
proverbs.practice: With little ones, one or two verses is plenty. You do not need the whole chapter to have the conversation.
proverbs.body:
Proverbs 21:3: to do what is right and just is more acceptable to the LORD than sacrifice. In other words, God is not impressed by the show.

He would rather have honest homework than a loud prayer, and a kept promise than a perfect church outfit.

proverbs.subject: Day 22: A good name and open hands
proverbs.title: A good name is worth more than riches, and generous people are blessed.
proverbs.focus: Family generosity project: pick something real this week. A bag of groceries for the food pantry, outgrown clothes, or a GiveSendGo campaign the kids help choose.
proverbs.prayer_focus:
If you could give one of your toys to a kid with none, which one would you give?
What makes someone a giver?
proverbs.prayer_verse:
Would you trade your reputation for money? People do it in small ways all the time. Where?
What do you have plenty of that someone else lacks: stuff, time, skill?
proverbs.practice: Let the kids ask the questions tonight. Hand a young reader the questions and let them run it.
proverbs.body:
Two anchors in chapter 22. Verse 1: a good name is more desirable than great riches. And verse 9: the generous will themselves be blessed, for they share their food with the poor.

Your name and your hands. Guard the first, open the second.

proverbs.subject: Day 23: Apply your heart
proverbs.title: Put your whole heart into learning, and do not envy people doing wrong.
proverbs.focus: Everyone names the one class, skill, or subject getting half their heart, and one way to give it a full heart this week.
proverbs.prayer_focus:
What is your favorite thing to learn about?
What does it mean to try with your whole heart?
proverbs.prayer_verse:
Where are you coasting right now, present but not really trying?
Who do you secretly envy, and what is the real cost of what they are doing?
proverbs.practice: Older kid not home? Text them the teen question and let them answer by text. It still counts.
proverbs.body:
Proverbs 23:12 says apply your heart to instruction and your ears to words of knowledge. Not just your seat in the chair, your heart.

And verse 17 warns: do not let your heart envy sinners. Shortcuts look shiny. They always cost more than they promise.

proverbs.subject: Day 24: By wisdom a house is built
proverbs.title: Wisdom builds a home and fills its rooms with good things.
proverbs.focus: Draw or describe your dream family room, then have each person name the invisible treasures they would fill it with.
proverbs.prayer_focus:
What is your favorite room in our house and why?
What treasure does our family have that money cannot buy?
proverbs.prayer_verse:
Verse 16 says the righteous fall seven times and rise again. What have you gotten back up from?
What rare and beautiful thing do you want your future home to be full of?
proverbs.practice: Missed a day or three? No guilt. Just do today's. The goal is talking about wisdom as a family, not a perfect streak.
proverbs.body:
Proverbs 24:3-4: by wisdom a house is built, and through understanding it is established; through knowledge its rooms are filled with rare and beautiful treasures.

The treasures that fill a home are not from the store. They are memories, safety, laughter, faith. That is what you have been building around this table and in this car all month.

proverbs.subject: Day 25: Self-control is your wall
proverbs.title: A person without self-control is a city with broken-down walls.
proverbs.focus: Everyone picks one self-control brick for the week and says it out loud. Check on each other kindly, no policing.
proverbs.prayer_focus:
Why did old cities have big walls?
What is something hard to stop doing once you start?
proverbs.prayer_verse:
Where is your wall broken right now: temper, phone, food, words?
What is one brick you could lay this week, one specific limit you set for yourself?
proverbs.practice: No table needed. The car works great: read the verses at pickup or on the way to practice and talk on the drive.
proverbs.body:
In Bible times, a city without walls was defenseless. Anything could walk in. Proverbs 25:28 says that is a person without self-control.

Self-control is not about being no fun. Walls are what make the fun inside safe.

proverbs.subject: Day 26: Do not feed the fire
proverbs.title: Without gossip, a quarrel dies down like a fire without wood.
proverbs.focus: Family rule proposal: we do not talk badly about people who are not in the room. Discuss it, adjust it, adopt it.
proverbs.prayer_focus:
What does a campfire need to keep burning?
What happens when we tattle just to get someone in trouble?
proverbs.prayer_verse:
Be honest: when friends start talking about someone, what do you usually do?
What quarrel in your world would die out if people just stopped feeding it?
proverbs.practice: Let a kid read the verses out loud. Kids remember what they read to the family far better than what they are read.
proverbs.body:
Proverbs 26:20: without wood a fire goes out; without gossip a quarrel dies down. Every conflict is a fire, and gossip is the firewood.

Families and friend groups stay at war because somebody keeps carrying wood. Be the one who puts the logs down.

proverbs.subject: Day 27: Iron sharpens iron
proverbs.title: As iron sharpens iron, so one person sharpens another.
proverbs.focus: Sharpening circle: each person tells the person on their right one strength they see in them, and one gentle push to grow.
proverbs.prayer_focus:
How do you make a pencil sharp? What happens to a dull one?
Who helps you get better at something?
proverbs.prayer_verse:
Who sharpens you, tells you the truth even when it stings?
Who are you sharpening? Or do you only hang out where there is no friction at all?
proverbs.practice: Play the chapter on the Bible app while everyone eats or rides. Audio counts.
proverbs.body:
Proverbs 27:17 is the friendship verse: as iron sharpens iron, so one person sharpens another. Sharpening involves friction. Sparks, even.

The people who make you better are not always the ones who make you comfortable. And verse 6 adds: wounds from a friend can be trusted.

proverbs.subject: Day 28: Bold as a lion
proverbs.title: The righteous are as bold as a lion, and confession brings mercy.
proverbs.focus: Courage round: everyone names one brave right thing they will do this week. Parents included. Follow up next week.
proverbs.prayer_focus:
What animal do you think is the bravest? Why?
Why does it feel better after you say sorry?
proverbs.prayer_verse:
What would you do this month if you were bold as a lion?
Is there anything you are carrying hidden? Verse 13 says mercy is on the other side of saying it.
proverbs.practice: Breakfast works as well as dinner. Attach it to a meal you already share.
proverbs.body:
Two lions in chapter 28. Verse 1: the righteous are as bold as a lion. Doing right gives you a spine.

And verse 13: whoever conceals their sins does not prosper, but the one who confesses and renounces them finds mercy. Hiding it eats you. Confessing it frees you.

proverbs.subject: Day 29: A fool gives full vent
proverbs.title: Fools give full vent to their rage, but the wise bring calm.
proverbs.focus: Build the family calm-down plan together: three steps anyone can use mid-meltdown. Post it where the meltdowns happen.
proverbs.prayer_focus:
What does your body feel like when you get really mad?
What helps you calm down?
proverbs.prayer_verse:
Are you a thermostat or a thermometer in this family?
What is your actual plan for the next time rage shows up? Name the steps.
proverbs.practice: With little ones, one or two verses is plenty. You do not need the whole chapter to have the conversation.
proverbs.body:
Proverbs 29:11: fools give full vent to their rage, but the wise bring calm in the end. Venting feels honest. Proverbs calls it foolish.

Bringing calm is not stuffing your feelings. It is being the thermostat instead of the thermometer, setting the temperature instead of just reporting it.

proverbs.subject: Day 30: Two honest prayers
proverbs.title: Give me neither poverty nor riches. Keep me honest and dependent on You.
proverbs.focus: Gratitude alphabet in the car or at the table: go A to Z naming things God gave your family. See how far you get.
proverbs.prayer_focus:
What are three things our family has that we can thank God for?
What is the difference between what you want and what you need?
proverbs.prayer_verse:
Would you honestly pray do not make me rich? Why is that hard?
What does enough look like for you?
proverbs.practice: Let the kids ask the questions tonight. Hand a young reader the questions and let them run it.
proverbs.body:
Proverbs 30 is a humble chapter. Agur admits what he does not know, then prays two things: keep lies far from me, and give me neither poverty nor riches, just my daily bread.

That prayer trusts God for enough. Not everything. Enough.

proverbs.subject: Day 31: A home built on wisdom
proverbs.title: A person and a family that fear the LORD are worth more than anything.
proverbs.focus: Celebrate. Special dessert or a drive for ice cream. Each person shares the one thing from Proverbs they want to carry for life. Then grab your certificate.
proverbs.prayer_focus:
What was your favorite day of this challenge?
What is one wise thing you learned this month?
proverbs.prayer_verse:
Which chapter actually changed something you did this month?
If your family kept one habit from these 31 days, which should it be?
proverbs.practice: Older kid not home? Text them the teen question and let them answer by text. It still counts.
proverbs.body:
The last chapter paints a person of strength and dignity whose family stands up and calls her blessed. The closing line of the whole book brings us back to day one: charm is deceptive and beauty is fleeting, but a person who fears the LORD is to be praised.

Thirty-one days. You read the entire book of wisdom together, around tables and in cars and wherever life happened. That is not a small thing. That is training hearts. Keep going, one conversation at a time.

james-drip.subject: One week until One Book Deep
james-drip.body:
Good morning, {{name}}.

One week from today, we begin.

One week from today, you and I start reading the entire book of James, every single day, for a month. Five chapters. About 15 minutes.

This is not a race to read more. It is a chance to go deep. To read one book so many times it becomes part of you.

This week, do two things. Pick the time you will read each morning. And tell one person you are doing this, so you are not doing it alone.

Your dashboard is ready whenever you want to look around.

See you on day one.

Heather

james-drip.subject: Three days. Is there someone who should join you?
james-drip.body:
Good morning, {{name}}.

Three days until One Book Deep.

Here is my one ask this morning. Is there someone who should do this with you? A friend, your sister, someone in your small group who has been wanting to get into the Word.

Text them the link. It is the easiest way to make sure you both finish.

heatherlynwilson.com/challenge-james

Three days. See who comes to mind.

Heather

james-drip.subject: Tomorrow we begin. James, every day.
james-drip.body:
Good morning, {{name}}.

Tomorrow we begin.

At 6am you will get your first email from me. Open it, then open your Bible to James chapter 1 and read all five chapters. Do not overthink it. Just read.

The same book, thirty-one times. Repetition is how the Word moves from your head to your heart.

I have been praying for this group. For you. For what God will say through James this month.

See you in the morning.

Heather

beatitudes-drip.subject: One week until we start hiding His word
beatitudes-drip.body:
Good morning, {{name}}.

One week from today, we start hiding His word in our hearts.

One week from today, we begin memorizing the Beatitudes, Matthew 5:1-12, one line at a time. By the end of the month you will be able to say the whole thing from memory.

This week, pick the time you will practice each day. Even five minutes is enough. And decide where you will post the words so you see them all day. The fridge, the mirror, the car.

Your dashboard is ready whenever you want to look around.

See you on day one.

Heather

beatitudes-drip.subject: Three days. Pick your translation, invite a friend.
beatitudes-drip.body:
Good morning, {{name}}.

Three days until we begin.

Memorizing sticks better with a friend. Is there someone who would love to hide the Beatitudes in their heart alongside you? Send them the link this morning.

heatherlynwilson.com/challenge-beatitudes

And if you have not picked your translation yet, open your dashboard and choose the one you want to learn. NIV, NLT, ESV, or KJV.

Three days.

Heather

beatitudes-drip.subject: Tomorrow. The first line.
beatitudes-drip.body:
Good morning, {{name}}.

Tomorrow we start.

At 6am you will get your first email from me, and we will begin with the whole picture before we learn the first line.

Here is what I love about memorizing Scripture. Once it is in you, no one can take it. It is there in the hard moments, the waiting, the times you do not know what to pray.

Thirty days from now, the Beatitudes will be yours for good.

See you in the morning.

Heather

proverbs-drip.subject: One week until Around the Table
proverbs-drip.body:
Good morning, {{name}}.

One week from today, your family starts Proverbs together.

One week from today we begin. One chapter a day, a big idea, a few questions for the kids, and one family challenge. Ten to fifteen minutes, and it counts even when it is messy.

This week, pick your moment. Around the table at dinner is great. So is the car on the way to school. Families are in the car more than they are around a table, and that works just fine. Have a kid read the verses out loud, or play the chapter on the Bible app while you drive.

Tell the kids it is coming. Kids do better when they know something is starting.

See you on day one.

Heather

proverbs-drip.subject: Three days. Know another family who should do this?
proverbs-drip.body:
Good morning, {{name}}.

Three days until Around the Table.

Here is my one ask this morning. Is there another family who should do this with yours? Cousins, neighbors, the family you sit near at church. Kids love knowing their friends are reading the same chapter.

Text them the link. It takes ten seconds.

heatherlynwilson.com/challenge-proverbs

Three days. See who comes to mind.

Heather

proverbs-drip.subject: Tomorrow we open Proverbs. Chapter 1.
proverbs-drip.body:
Good morning, {{name}}.

Tomorrow we begin.

In the morning you will get your first email from me. It has the chapter, the big idea, questions for your kids by age, and one family challenge for the day.

Do not aim for perfect. Aim for together. If dinner is chaos, do it in the car. If a kid rolls their eyes, keep going. If you miss a day, jump back in the next one. Thirty-one days of Proverbs will put more wisdom in your kids than a year of lectures.

I am praying for your family this month.

See you in the morning.

Heather

ot-90.subject: Week 1: In the beginning. Genesis and Exodus.
ot-90.body:
Good morning.

Welcome to the Old Testament in three months. This week is creation, the flood, Abraham, Jacob, Joseph, and the escape from Egypt. Ten chapters a day, and almost all of it is story.

Do not stop to study every detail. Just read and let it pull you in. This is the foundation everything else stands on.

Your dashboard has each day's chapters. I am reading with you.

Heather

ot-90.subject: Week 2: The wilderness years
ot-90.body:
Good morning.

This week you finish Exodus, walk through Leviticus, and get deep into Numbers. I will be honest: this is the stretch where people quit. All the laws and offerings can feel like a manual for a world that is gone.

Here is what to hold onto. Every rule exists because God wanted to live among His people. The whole section is Him saying, I want to be close, and here is how.

Push through. If you are still reading at the end of this week, you can finish the whole thing.

Heather

ot-90.subject: Week 3: Moses says goodbye, Joshua steps up
ot-90.body:
Good morning.

Big week. Moses gives his farewell speech in Deuteronomy, Joshua leads the people into the land, and Judges begins the long spiral of forgetting God and finding Him again.

Watch for one word over and over in Deuteronomy: remember. Moses knew what happens to people who forget what God has done. So do we.

Heather

ot-90.subject: Week 4: Judges, Ruth, and a shepherd king
ot-90.body:
Good morning.

This week has some of the best stories in the whole Bible. Gideon and Samson, Ruth's quiet faithfulness, Samuel hearing God's voice as a boy, David and Goliath, and David's rise and fall.

Notice that the Bible never cleans anyone up. David at his best and David at his worst are both on the page. That honesty is one of the reasons you can trust this book.

Heather

ot-90.subject: Week 5: Kings, temples, and a divided house
ot-90.body:
Good morning.

Solomon builds the temple this week, the kingdom splits in two, and Elijah stands alone against the prophets of Baal. Then Chronicles begins retelling the story with different eyes.

When you hit the name lists in Chronicles, do not stall out. Read them like a memorial wall, every name was a real person in God's story, and keep moving.

Heather

ot-90.subject: Week 6: Exile and the long road home
ot-90.body:
Good morning.

This week the kingdom falls, the temple burns, and the people are carried to Babylon. Then, seventy years later, they come home. Ezra rebuilds the temple, Nehemiah rebuilds the wall, and Esther risks her life for her people.

It is heavy reading and hopeful reading in the same week. Broken things get rebuilt. That is the whole point.

Heather

ot-90.subject: Week 7: Job and the songs begin
ot-90.body:
Good morning.

Job asks the hardest question in the Bible this week: why do good people suffer? And God answers, not with an explanation, but with Himself. Sometimes we do not get to know why. We get to know who.

Then the Psalms begin. Read them out loud when you can. They were written to be spoken.

Heather

ot-90.subject: Week 8: Deep in the Psalms
ot-90.body:
Good morning.

A whole week inside the Psalms. Crying out, praising, doubting, trusting, all of it mixed together, which is exactly what a real life with God looks like.

If one psalm grabs you this week, stop and read it twice. This is the one part of the plan where lingering is the point.

You are past halfway. I am proud of you.

Heather

ot-90.subject: Week 9: Wisdom for ordinary days
ot-90.body:
Good morning.

You finish the Psalms this week and walk into Proverbs, wisdom for money, words, work, friendship, and family. It is the most practical stretch of the whole Old Testament.

Try this: each day, pick one proverb and carry it around. Say it at dinner. Wisdom sticks when it gets used the same day.

Heather

ot-90.subject: Week 10: Ecclesiastes, the Song, and Isaiah begins
ot-90.body:
Good morning.

Ecclesiastes is the most honest book in the Bible, life without God is vapor, and it is not afraid to say so. The Song of Solomon celebrates love without blushing. And then Isaiah opens: judgment is coming, but so is a child, a servant, a King.

For unto us a child is born. You will read those words this week, written seven hundred years before Bethlehem.

Heather

ot-90.subject: Week 11: Comfort, and a weeping prophet
ot-90.body:
Good morning.

Isaiah 53 is this week. Read it slowly. He was pierced for our transgressions, crushed for our iniquities. It is the clearest picture of Jesus in the whole Old Testament.

Then Jeremiah, who preached his whole life to people who would not listen and kept going anyway. Faithfulness does not always look like success. Sometimes it just looks like showing up.

Heather

ot-90.subject: Week 12: Ruins, visions, and dry bones
ot-90.body:
Good morning.

Lamentations sits in the ruins of Jerusalem and still says: great is His faithfulness, His mercies are new every morning. That verse was not written on a good day. That is what makes it strong enough to hold you on a bad one.

Then Ezekiel's valley of dry bones, Daniel in the lions' den, and the beginning of the twelve small prophets. One week left.

Heather

ot-90.subject: Week 13: The last word, and then silence
ot-90.body:
Good morning.

This is your last week. Twelve short prophets, each with one urgent thing to say. Micah tells you what God requires: do justice, love mercy, walk humbly. Habakkuk decides to rejoice even if everything fails. Malachi gets the last word, and then four hundred years of silence, waiting for a voice in the wilderness.

You read the entire Old Testament in three months. Very few people ever do that. When you finish, your certificate is waiting on your dashboard.

I am so proud of you. Thank you for reading alongside me.

With love,
Heather

nt-90.subject: Week 1: Jesus arrives. Matthew begins.
nt-90.body:
Good morning.

Welcome to the New Testament in three months. Three chapters a day, about ten minutes, slow enough to actually chew on what you read.

This week is the birth of Jesus, His baptism, the Sermon on the Mount, and miracle after miracle. Watch how He treats people the world overlooked. That thread runs through everything.

Your dashboard has each day's chapters. I am reading with you.

Heather

nt-90.subject: Week 2: The cross, and a second witness
nt-90.body:
Good morning.

This week you walk through the last days of Jesus in Matthew, the cross, the empty tomb, and the great commission, and then Mark starts the story again at a sprint. Mark's favorite word is immediately. Everything moves.

Reading two accounts back to back is not repetition. It is two witnesses, and each one sees things the other does not.

Heather

nt-90.subject: Week 3: Mark finishes, Luke slows down
nt-90.body:
Good morning.

Mark ends at the empty tomb and Luke begins with the fullest telling of all, he interviewed eyewitnesses and wrote it down carefully. This week you get the manger, the shepherds, and then the parables only Luke kept: the good Samaritan, and the prodigal son.

The father running down the road to meet his ruined boy. That is God, and that is the whole gospel in one picture.

Heather

nt-90.subject: Week 4: Luke ends, John goes deep
nt-90.body:
Good morning.

Luke carries you through the cross and resurrection this week, and then John changes the pace entirely. John is the gospel that soars: in the beginning was the Word. Bread of life. Light of the world. The raising of Lazarus.

Four tellings, one Jesus. By the end of this week you will have read the heart of all four gospels.

Heather

nt-90.subject: Week 5: The church catches fire
nt-90.body:
Good morning.

This week Jesus prays for you, that is John 17, goes to the cross, and rises. Then Acts: the Spirit falls, Peter preaches, the church explodes, Stephen dies with his face like an angel, and Saul the persecutor meets Jesus on a road.

Acts reads like an adventure novel, except every word of it happened.

Heather

nt-90.subject: Week 6: To the ends of the earth, and Romans begins
nt-90.body:
Good morning.

Paul sets out this week, shipwrecks, prisons, riots, and the gospel spreading through all of it. Acts ends with the message unstoppable, and then Romans begins, the deepest book in the New Testament.

Take Romans slowly. Three chapters a day is exactly the right pace for it.

Heather

nt-90.subject: Week 7: Grace, all the way down
nt-90.body:
Good morning.

Romans 8 is this week. There is now no condemnation. Nothing can separate us from the love of God. Some people say it is the greatest chapter in the Bible. Read it twice.

Then First Corinthians: Paul writing to a church that was a mess, and loving them anyway. Sound familiar? Church has never been tidy. Grace has always been the point.

Heather

nt-90.subject: Week 8: Love, resurrection, and treasure in clay jars
nt-90.body:
Good morning.

Love is patient, love is kind. Paul did not write that for weddings. He wrote it for a church tearing itself apart. Then the resurrection chapter, and Second Corinthians, where Paul opens his own wounds: treasure in jars of clay, strength made perfect in weakness.

You are past halfway. Keep showing up.

Heather

nt-90.subject: Week 9: Freedom and identity
nt-90.body:
Good morning.

Four letters this week, and each one hands you something. Galatians: you are free, do not go back to earning it. Ephesians: who you are in Christ, chosen, adopted, loved. Philippians: joy, written from a prison cell. Colossians: Christ above everything.

These are short enough to read in one sitting and deep enough to live in for years.

Heather

nt-90.subject: Week 10: Hope, and a charge to keep
nt-90.reading: Days 64 to 70: 1 Thessalonians 1–3 through 2 Timothy 4, Titus 1–2
nt-90.body:
Good morning.

The Thessalonian letters are about hope, He is coming back, so live ready. Then Paul's letters to his young pastors, Timothy and Titus. Second Timothy is the last thing Paul ever wrote: I have fought the good fight, I have finished the race, I have kept the faith.

That is the goal. Not a perfect race. A finished one.

Heather

nt-90.subject: Week 11: A better covenant, a working faith
nt-90.reading: Days 71 to 77: Titus 3, Philemon 1, Hebrews 1 through James 4–5
nt-90.body:
Good morning.

Hebrews is this week, Jesus is better than angels, better than Moses, better than every sacrifice, and chapter 11 is the faith hall of fame. By faith Abraham. By faith Moses. By faith Rahab. You have read all their stories now.

Then James, faith that rolls up its sleeves. If you ever do the One Book Deep challenge, this little book is the one we live in for a month.

Heather

nt-90.subject: Week 12: Living stones, and heaven opens
nt-90.body:
Good morning.

Peter writes to scattered, suffering believers: you are chosen, you are living stones, do not be surprised by fire. John writes: God is love, and love one another. And then Revelation opens, and heaven's throne room comes into view.

Do not read Revelation to decode it. Read it to worship. That is what it is for.

Heather

nt-90.subject: Week 13: All things new
nt-90.body:
Good morning.

Your last week. Revelation to the very end: the battle, the fall of every evil thing, and then a new heaven and a new earth. No more tears. No more death. The story that started in a garden ends in a city with God dwelling among His people forever.

You read the entire New Testament in three months, and you did not skim it. You walked it.

When you finish day 90, your certificate is on your dashboard. I am so proud of you. Thank you for reading alongside me.

With love,
Heather

thanks.subject: Day 1: Two ways to live
thanks.title: Two ways to live
thanks.practice: Thank God for two places He has rooted you: a person and a place.
thanks.body:
Good morning.

Psalm 1 opens the whole book with a choice: a tree planted by streams, or chaff the wind blows away. Rooted people are thankful people, because they know where their water comes from.

thanks.subject: Day 2: What is man?
thanks.title: What is man?
thanks.practice: Step outside or look out a window. Thank Him for three things He made.
thanks.body:
Good morning.

David looks up at the night sky and cannot believe God bothers with us. He made the moon and the stars, and He is mindful of you.

thanks.subject: Day 3: Honest and hopeful
thanks.title: Honest and hopeful
thanks.practice: Thank God for one hard season He carried you through.
thanks.body:
Good morning.

Psalm 13 starts with How long, O Lord? and ends with singing. Gratitude does not mean pretending. It means finishing the sentence the way David does: But I trust in your unfailing love.

thanks.subject: Day 4: A good inheritance
thanks.title: A good inheritance
thanks.practice: Name three ordinary things about your life you would miss terribly.
thanks.body:
Good morning.

The boundary lines have fallen for me in pleasant places. David is thankful for the life he actually has, not the one he might have had.

thanks.subject: Day 5: The Shepherd
thanks.title: The Shepherd
thanks.practice: Pick three gifts straight out of Psalm 23 and thank Him for your version of them.
thanks.body:
Good morning.

You know this one by heart. Read it slowly anyway. Every line is something to be thankful for: rest, guidance, presence in the valley, a table, a cup running over.

thanks.subject: Day 6: Joy in the morning
thanks.title: Joy in the morning
thanks.practice: Thank God for a morning that came after a long night.
thanks.body:
Good morning.

Weeping may stay for the night, but joy comes in the morning. David wrote this at a dedication, looking back at what God brought him through.

thanks.subject: Day 7: Taste and see
thanks.title: Taste and see
thanks.practice: Thank Him for a prayer He answered, even one you had forgotten you prayed.
thanks.body:
Good morning.

I sought the Lord, and he answered me and delivered me from all my fears. Psalm 34 invites you to test the goodness of God like you would taste a meal.

thanks.subject: Day 8: Out of the pit
thanks.title: Out of the pit
thanks.practice: Thank God for where you are not anymore.
thanks.body:
Good morning.

He lifted me out of the slimy pit and set my feet on a rock and put a new song in my mouth. That is a testimony in one verse.

thanks.subject: Day 9: Thirsty
thanks.title: Thirsty
thanks.practice: Thank God for the hunger itself, that you want more of Him at all.
thanks.body:
Good morning.

As the deer pants for streams of water, so my soul pants for you. Even the wanting is a gift, because it means there is a stream.

thanks.subject: Day 10: A very present help
thanks.title: A very present help
thanks.practice: Thank Him for the trouble that did not swallow you.
thanks.body:
Good morning.

God is our refuge and strength, an ever-present help in trouble. Therefore we will not fear, though the earth give way. Therefore is the thankful word in that verse.

thanks.subject: Day 11: A clean heart
thanks.title: A clean heart
thanks.practice: Thank God for one specific thing He has forgiven you for.
thanks.body:
Good morning.

Psalm 51 is David at his worst, asking for mercy. The most thankful people are forgiven people who know it.

thanks.subject: Day 12: Under His wings
thanks.title: Under His wings
thanks.practice: Thank Him for the shelter you are under right now: home, church, friendship.
thanks.body:
Good morning.

David wrote this hiding in a cave, and still says: I will take refuge in the shadow of your wings until the disaster has passed. Gratitude can live in a cave.

thanks.subject: Day 13: The overflowing cart
thanks.title: The overflowing cart
thanks.practice: Thank God for three things on your table this week.
thanks.body:
Good morning.

You crown the year with your bounty, and your carts overflow with abundance. Psalm 65 is the harvest psalm, and November is the harvest month.

thanks.subject: Day 14: Come and hear
thanks.title: Come and hear
thanks.practice: Tell one person today something God has done for you. Then write it down.
thanks.body:
Good morning.

Come and hear, all you who fear God; let me tell you what he has done for me. Gratitude is meant to be said out loud to somebody.

thanks.subject: Day 15: Nothing on earth
thanks.title: Nothing on earth
thanks.practice: Thank God for something money did not buy.
thanks.body:
Good morning.

Whom have I in heaven but you? And earth has nothing I desire besides you. Asaph almost lost his footing envying others, until he got honest about what he actually had.

thanks.subject: Day 16: Remember the deeds
thanks.title: Remember the deeds
thanks.practice: Write down three things God did for you in years past.
thanks.body:
Good morning.

I will remember the deeds of the Lord. When Asaph could not feel God in the present, he thanked Him for the past, and it steadied him.

thanks.subject: Day 17: Better is one day
thanks.title: Better is one day
thanks.practice: Thank God for your church, or the people who are church to you.
thanks.body:
Good morning.

Better is one day in your courts than a thousand elsewhere. The sparrow found a home near the altar. So did you.

thanks.subject: Day 18: Teach us to number
thanks.title: Teach us to number
thanks.practice: Thank God for your age, exactly the number it is, and one gift that came with it.
thanks.body:
Good morning.

Teach us to number our days, that we may gain a heart of wisdom. Moses wrote this one. Counting days and counting blessings turn out to be the same skill.

thanks.subject: Day 19: Under His feathers
thanks.title: Under His feathers
thanks.practice: Thank God for protection you never saw, the near misses you slept through.
thanks.body:
Good morning.

He will cover you with his feathers, and under his wings you will find refuge. Someone you love has been kept safe more times than you know.

thanks.subject: Day 20: Enter with thanksgiving
thanks.title: Enter with thanksgiving
thanks.practice: Thank Him today for who He is, not what He gives. Three things about Him.
thanks.body:
Good morning.

Enter his gates with thanksgiving and his courts with praise. Psalm 100 is five verses long. Read it twice, once quietly and once out loud.

thanks.subject: Day 21: Forget not
thanks.title: Forget not
thanks.practice: Borrow David's list. Which three of his benefits are yours today?
thanks.body:
Good morning.

Praise the Lord, my soul, and forget not all his benefits. Then David lists them: forgiveness, healing, redemption, love, renewal. This psalm is a gratitude list with a melody.

thanks.subject: Day 22: Let the redeemed say so
thanks.title: Let the redeemed say so
thanks.practice: Say so. Thank God in writing for the deliverance story only you can tell.
thanks.body:
Good morning.

Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good. Four times in this psalm, people in trouble cry out, He delivers them, and then: let them give thanks. That is the pattern of a whole life.

thanks.subject: Day 23: From the rising of the sun
thanks.title: From the rising of the sun
thanks.practice: Thank God for a time He met you when you were low.
thanks.body:
Good morning.

From the rising of the sun to the place where it sets, the name of the Lord is to be praised. He raises the poor from the dust. God stoops low, and that is worth everything.

thanks.subject: Day 24: This is the day
thanks.title: This is the day
thanks.practice: Thank God for today. Not a better day, this one. Three reasons.
thanks.body:
Good morning.

This is the day the Lord has made; let us rejoice and be glad in it. Psalm 118 was likely the hymn Jesus sang on the night He was betrayed. He gave thanks that night too.

thanks.subject: Day 25: He watches over you
thanks.title: He watches over you
thanks.practice: Thank God for safe travels and quiet nights, this week and this year.
thanks.body:
Good morning.

He who watches over you will not slumber. Every trip you took this year, every night you slept, He was awake.

thanks.subject: Day 26: Filled with laughter
thanks.title: Filled with laughter
thanks.practice: At the table today, let everyone answer: what great thing has He done for us this year?
thanks.body:
Good morning.

Our mouths were filled with laughter, our tongues with songs of joy. The Lord has done great things for us. Happy Thanksgiving. This psalm was written for a day exactly like today.

thanks.subject: Day 27: Servants by night
thanks.title: Servants by night
thanks.practice: Thank God for the people who serve while you sleep, and name a few.
thanks.body:
Good morning.

Psalm 134 is three verses, sung by those keeping watch in the temple at night. Even the night shift blesses the Lord.

thanks.subject: Day 28: His love endures forever
thanks.title: His love endures forever
thanks.practice: Write your own three verses. Three moments from your life, each ending: His love endures forever.
thanks.body:
Good morning.

Twenty-six verses, and every one ends the same way: His love endures forever. Creation, rescue, provision, all of it hangs on that one refrain.

thanks.subject: Day 29: One generation to another
thanks.title: One generation to another
thanks.practice: Thank God for the person who first told you about Him, by name.
thanks.body:
Good morning.

One generation commends your works to another. Someone told you about God. Someone will hear it from you.

thanks.subject: Day 30: Let everything that has breath
thanks.title: Let everything that has breath
thanks.practice: Read back through your whole month of thanks. Then add the final three.
thanks.body:
Good morning.

The book ends with nothing but praise. No requests, no complaints, just six verses of hallelujah. You have breath. That is the last reason on the list, and the first.
