psalms-150.title: Under His wings
psalms-150.practice: Thank Him for the shelter you are under right now: home, church, friendship.
psalms-150.body:
Good morning.

David wrote this hiding in a cave, and still says: I will take refuge in the shadow of your wings until the disaster has passed. Gratitude can live in a cave.

Today's chapters are Psalms 56 to 60, with Psalm 57 as the heart of the day.

psalms-150.subject: Day 13: The overflowing cart
psalms-150.title: The overflowing cart
psalms-150.practice: Thank God for three things on your table this week.
psalms-150.body:
Good morning.

You crown the year with your bounty, and your carts overflow with abundance. Psalm 65 is the harvest psalm, and November is the harvest month.

Today's chapters are Psalms 61 to 65, with Psalm 65 as the heart of the day.

psalms-150.subject: Day 14: Come and hear
psalms-150.title: Come and hear
psalms-150.practice: Tell one person today something God has done for you. Then write it down.
psalms-150.body:
Good morning.

Come and hear, all you who fear God; let me tell you what he has done for me. Gratitude is meant to be said out loud to somebody.

Today's chapters are Psalms 66 to 70, with Psalm 66 as the heart of the day.

psalms-150.subject: Day 15: Nothing on earth
psalms-150.title: Nothing on earth
psalms-150.practice: Thank God for something money did not buy.
psalms-150.body:
Good morning.

Whom have I in heaven but you? And earth has nothing I desire besides you. Asaph almost lost his footing envying others, until he got honest about what he actually had.

Today's chapters are Psalms 71 to 75, with Psalm 73 as the heart of the day.

psalms-150.subject: Day 16: Remember the deeds
psalms-150.title: Remember the deeds
psalms-150.practice: Write down three things God did for you in years past.
psalms-150.body:
Good morning.

I will remember the deeds of the Lord. When Asaph could not feel God in the present, he thanked Him for the past, and it steadied him.

Today's chapters are Psalms 76 to 80, with Psalm 77 as the heart of the day.

psalms-150.subject: Day 17: Better is one day
psalms-150.title: Better is one day
psalms-150.practice: Thank God for your church, or the people who are church to you.
psalms-150.body:
Good morning.

Better is one day in your courts than a thousand elsewhere. The sparrow found a home near the altar. So did you.

Today's chapters are Psalms 81 to 85, with Psalm 84 as the heart of the day.

psalms-150.subject: Day 18: Teach us to number
psalms-150.title: Teach us to number
psalms-150.practice: Thank God for your age, exactly the number it is, and one gift that came with it.
psalms-150.body:
Good morning.

Teach us to number our days, that we may gain a heart of wisdom. Moses wrote this one. Counting days and counting blessings turn out to be the same skill.

Today's chapters are Psalms 86 to 90, with Psalm 90 as the heart of the day.

psalms-150.subject: Day 19: Under His feathers
psalms-150.title: Under His feathers
psalms-150.practice: Thank God for protection you never saw, the near misses you slept through.
psalms-150.body:
Good morning.

He will cover you with his feathers, and under his wings you will find refuge. Someone you love has been kept safe more times than you know.

Today's chapters are Psalms 91 to 95, with Psalm 91 as the heart of the day.

psalms-150.subject: Day 20: Enter with thanksgiving
psalms-150.title: Enter with thanksgiving
psalms-150.practice: Thank Him today for who He is, not what He gives. Three things about Him.
psalms-150.body:
Good morning.

Enter his gates with thanksgiving and his courts with praise. Psalm 100 is five verses long. Read it twice, once quietly and once out loud.

Today's chapters are Psalms 96 to 100, with Psalm 100 as the heart of the day.

psalms-150.subject: Day 21: Forget not
psalms-150.title: Forget not
psalms-150.practice: Borrow David's list. Which three of his benefits are yours today?
psalms-150.body:
Good morning.

Praise the Lord, my soul, and forget not all his benefits. Then David lists them: forgiveness, healing, redemption, love, renewal. This psalm is a gratitude list with a melody.

Today's chapters are Psalms 101 to 105, with Psalm 103 as the heart of the day.

psalms-150.subject: Day 22: Let the redeemed say so
psalms-150.title: Let the redeemed say so
psalms-150.practice: Say so. Thank God in writing for the deliverance story only you can tell.
psalms-150.body:
Good morning.

Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good. Four times in this psalm, people in trouble cry out, He delivers them, and then: let them give thanks. That is the pattern of a whole life.

Today's chapters are Psalms 106 to 110, with Psalm 107 as the heart of the day.

psalms-150.subject: Day 23: From the rising of the sun
psalms-150.title: From the rising of the sun
psalms-150.practice: Thank God for a time He met you when you were low.
psalms-150.body:
Good morning.

From the rising of the sun to the place where it sets, the name of the Lord is to be praised. He raises the poor from the dust. God stoops low, and that is worth everything.

Today's chapters are Psalms 111 to 115, with Psalm 113 as the heart of the day.

psalms-150.subject: Day 24: This is the day
psalms-150.title: This is the day
psalms-150.practice: Thank God for today. Not a better day, this one. Three reasons.
psalms-150.body:
Good morning.

This is the day the Lord has made; let us rejoice and be glad in it. Psalm 118 was likely the hymn Jesus sang on the night He was betrayed. He gave thanks that night too.

Today's chapters are Psalms 116 to 120, with Psalm 118 as the heart of the day.

psalms-150.subject: Day 25: He watches over you
psalms-150.title: He watches over you
psalms-150.practice: Thank God for safe travels and quiet nights, this week and this year.
psalms-150.body:
Good morning.

He who watches over you will not slumber. Every trip you took this year, every night you slept, He was awake.

Today's chapters are Psalms 121 to 125, with Psalm 121 as the heart of the day.

psalms-150.subject: Day 26: Filled with laughter
psalms-150.title: Filled with laughter
psalms-150.practice: At the table today, let everyone answer: what great thing has He done for us this year?
psalms-150.body:
Good morning.

Our mouths were filled with laughter, our tongues with songs of joy. The Lord has done great things for us. Happy Thanksgiving. This psalm was written for a day exactly like today.

Today's chapters are Psalms 126 to 130, with Psalm 126 as the heart of the day.

psalms-150.subject: Day 27: Servants by night
psalms-150.title: Servants by night
psalms-150.practice: Thank God for the people who serve while you sleep, and name a few.
psalms-150.body:
Good morning.

Psalm 134 is three verses, sung by those keeping watch in the temple at night. Even the night shift blesses the Lord.

Today's chapters are Psalms 131 to 135, with Psalm 134 as the heart of the day.

psalms-150.subject: Day 28: His love endures forever
psalms-150.title: His love endures forever
psalms-150.practice: Write your own three verses. Three moments from your life, each ending: His love endures forever.
psalms-150.body:
Good morning.

Twenty-six verses, and every one ends the same way: His love endures forever. Creation, rescue, provision, all of it hangs on that one refrain.

Today's chapters are Psalms 136 to 140, with Psalm 136 as the heart of the day.

psalms-150.subject: Day 29: One generation to another
psalms-150.title: One generation to another
psalms-150.practice: Thank God for the person who first told you about Him, by name.
psalms-150.body:
Good morning.

One generation commends your works to another. Someone told you about God. Someone will hear it from you.

Today's chapters are Psalms 141 to 145, with Psalm 145 as the heart of the day.

psalms-150.subject: Day 30: Let everything that has breath
psalms-150.title: Let everything that has breath
psalms-150.practice: Read back through your whole month of thanks. Then add the final three.
psalms-150.body:
Good morning.

The book ends with nothing but praise. No requests, no complaints, just six verses of hallelujah. You have breath. That is the last reason on the list, and the first.

Today's chapters are Psalms 146 to 150, with Psalm 150 as the heart of the day.

gospels.subject: Day 1: Immediately
gospels.title: Immediately
gospels.body:
Good morning.

Mark wastes no time. By chapter three Jesus has been baptized, tempted, called the twelve, healed crowds, and made the religious leaders furious. Mark's favorite word is immediately. Watch what Jesus does before anyone explains who He is.

gospels.subject: Day 2: Even the wind obeys
gospels.title: Even the wind obeys
gospels.body:
Good morning.

He calms a storm with a word, raises a little girl, feeds five thousand, and walks on the sea. The disciples keep asking the right question: who is this? Hold that question. It is the whole month.

gospels.subject: Day 3: Who do you say I am
gospels.title: Who do you say I am
gospels.body:
Good morning.

Halfway through Mark, Jesus asks the question straight out, and Peter answers: You are the Messiah. Then Jesus starts explaining what kind of Messiah He is, one who will suffer. Nobody expected that.

gospels.subject: Day 4: The servant King
gospels.title: The servant King
gospels.body:
Good morning.

The Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many. That is Mark's whole gospel in one verse. It is Jesus explaining His own death before it happens.

gospels.subject: Day 5: The night before
gospels.title: The night before
gospels.body:
Good morning.

The last supper, Gethsemane, the arrest, the trial. Jesus prays: not what I will, but what you will. Everyone deserts Him. Peter denies Him. He goes forward alone, on purpose.

gospels.subject: Day 6: The tomb is empty
gospels.title: The tomb is empty
gospels.body:
Good morning.

The centurion who watched Him die says it first: surely this man was the Son of God. And then the stone is rolled away. Mark ends in wonder and fear, because what do you do with an empty tomb? Tomorrow, John starts answering.

gospels.subject: Day 7: The Word became flesh
gospels.title: The Word became flesh
gospels.body:
Good morning.

John does not start in Bethlehem. He starts before creation. In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was God, and the Word became flesh and dwelt among us. Everything Mark showed you, John now explains.

gospels.subject: Day 8: So loved the world
gospels.title: So loved the world
gospels.body:
Good morning.

For God so loved the world that he gave his one and only Son. You have heard the verse your whole life. Read it today in its own house, in a midnight conversation with a confused religious man.

gospels.subject: Day 9: Bread and light
gospels.title: Bread and light
gospels.body:
Good morning.

I am the bread of life. I am the light of the world. Jesus does not just give bread and light, He is them. John gives you seven I am statements this month. Start collecting them.

gospels.subject: Day 10: Resurrection and life
gospels.title: Resurrection and life
gospels.body:
Good morning.

A man born blind sees. Lazarus walks out of his tomb. And Jesus says the biggest thing anyone has ever said: I am the resurrection and the life. Then John adds the shortest verse in the Bible: Jesus wept. Both are true of Him.

gospels.subject: Day 11: The way
gospels.title: The way
gospels.body:
Good morning.

The upper room. He washes their feet, then says: I am the way and the truth and the life. Let not your hearts be troubled. These three chapters have carried more people through more dark nights than any pages ever written.

gospels.subject: Day 12: The vine and the prayer
gospels.title: The vine and the prayer
gospels.body:
Good morning.

I am the vine; you are the branches. Then chapter 17: Jesus prays, and He prays for you. My prayer is not for them alone. I pray also for those who will believe in me through their message. That is us.

gospels.subject: Day 13: It is finished
gospels.title: It is finished
gospels.body:
Good morning.

Pilate asks, What is truth? while Truth stands in front of him. Jesus carries His own cross, and His last word is a single word in Greek: finished. Not defeated. Finished, like a work completed.

gospels.subject: Day 14: Do you love me
gospels.title: Do you love me
gospels.body:
Good morning.

Mary hears her name and knows Him. Thomas gets his proof and falls down: my Lord and my God. And Peter, who denied Him three times, gets asked three times: do you love me? Then feed my sheep. Failure is not the end of the story.

gospels.subject: Day 15: The family tree
gospels.title: The family tree
gospels.body:
Good morning.

Matthew opens with a genealogy because his whole point is a promise kept: son of David, son of Abraham. You get your first taste of Christmas today, wise men and a star, and a king so threatened by a baby he shakes.

gospels.subject: Day 16: The sermon
gospels.title: The sermon
gospels.body:
Good morning.

The Sermon on the Mount, all of it in one sitting. The Beatitudes, salt and light, the Lord's Prayer, the two builders. If you did September's challenge, chapter five will feel like coming home.

gospels.subject: Day 17: Authority
gospels.title: Authority
gospels.body:
Good morning.

Leprosy, storms, demons, paralysis, death. Nothing outranks Him. And then the gentlest verse in Matthew: Come to me, all you who are weary and burdened, and I will give you rest.

gospels.subject: Day 18: Something greater
gospels.title: Something greater
gospels.body:
Good morning.

The kingdom parables: the sower, the mustard seed, the treasure hidden in a field. The kingdom of heaven starts small and quiet and ends up filling everything. Which is also the Christmas story, if you think about it.

gospels.subject: Day 19: Keys of the kingdom
gospels.title: Keys of the kingdom
gospels.body:
Good morning.

Peter says it plainly: You are the Messiah, the Son of the living God. The transfiguration follows, a glimpse of the King in His glory. And then Jesus teaches about forgiveness, seventy times seven.

gospels.subject: Day 20: The King arrives
gospels.title: The King arrives
gospels.body:
Good morning.

Palm Sunday. The King enters His city, on a donkey, while children shout hosanna. Zechariah promised exactly this five hundred years earlier. Matthew keeps saying it: this was to fulfill what was spoken.

gospels.subject: Day 21: The greatest commandment
gospels.title: The greatest commandment
gospels.body:
Good morning.

Love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind. And love your neighbor as yourself. Everything hangs on these two. The King tells you plainly what His kingdom runs on.

gospels.subject: Day 22: All authority
gospels.title: All authority
gospels.body:
Good morning.

The cross, the empty tomb, and the mountain in Galilee: All authority in heaven and on earth has been given to me. Go. You have now read three witnesses. Tomorrow, Luke sits you down for the story you have been waiting for.

gospels.subject: Day 23: The angel and the girl
gospels.title: The angel and the girl
gospels.body:
Good morning.

Three weeks of walking with Jesus, and now Luke takes you back to the very beginning. An old priest struck silent, and a teenage girl who says: I am the Lord's servant. May your word to me be fulfilled. Mary's song will stay with you all day.

gospels.subject: Day 24: The manger
gospels.title: The manger
gospels.body:
Good morning.

Christmas Eve, and the reading is the Christmas story. The census, the stable, the shepherds, the angels: glory to God in the highest. You know who this baby is now. Mark showed you, John told you, Matthew proved it. Read it slowly tonight, out loud if you can.

gospels.subject: Day 25: Christmas Day
gospels.title: Christmas Day
gospels.body:
Good morning.

Merry Christmas. The baby grows up: baptized, tempted, and standing in His hometown synagogue reading Isaiah: The Spirit of the Lord is on me, because he has anointed me to proclaim good news to the poor. Today that scripture is fulfilled. That is what Christmas set in motion.

gospels.subject: Day 26: Friend of sinners
gospels.title: Friend of sinners
gospels.body:
Good morning.

Luke loves the outsiders: fishermen, tax collectors, a centurion, a sinful woman washing His feet with her tears. Your faith has saved you; go in peace. Nobody is beneath His notice, which is very good news.

gospels.subject: Day 27: The good Samaritan
gospels.title: The good Samaritan
gospels.body:
Good morning.

Only Luke kept the good Samaritan. Go and do likewise. And only Luke kept Mary and Martha, one distracted, one at His feet. In a week between holidays, those two sisters are worth sitting with.

gospels.subject: Day 28: Teach us to pray
gospels.title: Teach us to pray
gospels.body:
Good morning.

The disciples watch Jesus pray and ask for lessons. Do not worry about your life. Consider the ravens. Consider the lilies. Your Father knows what you need. December is a worried month; these chapters are the antidote.

gospels.subject: Day 29: Lost and found
gospels.title: Lost and found
gospels.body:
Good morning.

The lost sheep, the lost coin, the lost son. Three stories, one point: heaven throws a party when anyone comes home. The father running down the road is the clearest picture of God in the whole Bible.

gospels.subject: Day 30: The King and the tax man
gospels.title: The King and the tax man
gospels.body:
Good morning.

Zacchaeus climbs a tree and Jesus invites Himself to dinner: the Son of Man came to seek and to save the lost. Then Jerusalem, tears over the city, and the temple cleared. The road is pointing toward the cross now.

gospels.subject: Day 31: The road to Emmaus
gospels.title: The road to Emmaus
gospels.body:
Good morning.

The last day of the year: the cross, the tomb, and two travelers on a road whose hearts burn as a stranger opens the Scriptures. Then they recognize Him. You have read four gospels in a month. May you walk into the new year the same way they walked back to Jerusalem: hearts burning, running to tell someone.

luke.subject: Day 1: The angel and the girl
luke.title: The angel and the girl
luke.body:
Good morning.

An old priest struck silent and a teenage girl who says yes: I am the Lord's servant. One chapter a day, and you will finish the whole story of Jesus by Christmas Eve.

luke.subject: Day 2: The manger, early
luke.title: The manger, early
luke.body:
Good morning.

You get the Christmas story on December 2, and you will get to read it again with new eyes on Christmas Eve when you finish the book. The shepherds went and told everyone. That is still the assignment.

luke.subject: Day 3: The voice
luke.title: The voice
luke.body:
Good morning.

John the Baptist prepares the way, and at Jesus' baptism the Father speaks: You are my Son, whom I love. Everything starts from being loved.

luke.subject: Day 4: Tempted and anointed
luke.title: Tempted and anointed
luke.body:
Good morning.

Jesus faces the tempter with nothing but Scripture, then announces His mission in His hometown: good news to the poor, freedom for the prisoners. They loved it until they realized He meant it.

luke.subject: Day 5: Deep water
luke.title: Deep water
luke.body:
Good morning.

Put out into deep water. Peter had fished all night and caught nothing, but at His word he let down the nets. Do not be afraid; from now on you will fish for people.

luke.subject: Day 6: Level ground
luke.title: Level ground
luke.body:
Good morning.

Luke's sermon on the plain: love your enemies, do good to those who hate you. Blessed are you who are poor. It is the upside down kingdom, stated flat out.

luke.subject: Day 7: Your faith has saved you
luke.title: Your faith has saved you
luke.body:
Good morning.

A centurion's servant, a widow's son, and a sinful woman weeping at His feet while the religious men squirm. Jesus sees her, and says so. He sees you too.

luke.subject: Day 8: Storms and legions
luke.title: Storms and legions
luke.body:
Good morning.

He calms a storm, frees a tormented man, heals a bleeding woman, and raises a little girl. Who is this? Even the wind and the water obey him. Keep asking.

luke.subject: Day 9: Who do you say I am
luke.title: Who do you say I am
luke.body:
Good morning.

Peter answers the question of the whole book: God's Messiah. The transfiguration follows. Listen to him, the Father says. That is still the best advice ever given.

luke.subject: Day 10: The Samaritan
luke.title: The Samaritan
luke.body:
Good morning.

Go and do likewise. And then Mary at His feet: only one thing is needed. Busy season, this chapter. Read it twice.

luke.subject: Day 11: Teach us to pray
luke.title: Teach us to pray
luke.body:
Good morning.

The Lord's Prayer, and a Father who gives good gifts. Ask and it will be given to you; seek and you will find.

luke.subject: Day 12: Do not worry
luke.title: Do not worry
luke.body:
Good morning.

Consider the ravens. Consider the lilies. Do not be afraid, little flock, for your Father has been pleased to give you the kingdom. December needs this chapter.

luke.subject: Day 13: The narrow door
luke.title: The narrow door
luke.body:
Good morning.

A crippled woman stands straight after eighteen years, and Jesus grieves over Jerusalem like a hen gathering chicks. He has wanted to gather you for a long time.

luke.subject: Day 14: The great banquet
luke.title: The great banquet
luke.body:
Good morning.

Invite the poor, the crippled, the lame, the blind, and you will be blessed. The kingdom is a feast, and the guest list is longer than anyone expected.

luke.subject: Day 15: Lost and found
luke.title: Lost and found
luke.body:
Good morning.

The sheep, the coin, the son. The father runs. If you only had one chapter of Luke, it would be this one.

luke.subject: Day 16: Two masters
luke.title: Two masters
luke.body:
Good morning.

You cannot serve both God and money. Luke never lets us look away from what we do with what we have. Neither should we.

luke.subject: Day 17: One came back
luke.title: One came back
luke.body:
Good morning.

Ten healed, one thankful. Where are the other nine? After a month of gratitude in November, this chapter reads differently.

luke.subject: Day 18: Like a child
luke.title: Like a child
luke.body:
Good morning.

Anyone who will not receive the kingdom of God like a little child will never enter it. The blind beggar shouts louder when the crowd tells him to hush. Good strategy.

luke.subject: Day 19: Zacchaeus
luke.title: Zacchaeus
luke.body:
Good morning.

The Son of Man came to seek and to save the lost. Then the King rides into Jerusalem on a donkey while the stones almost cry out.

luke.subject: Day 20: Whose image
luke.title: Whose image
luke.body:
Good morning.

Give back to Caesar what is Caesar's, and to God what is God's. The coin bears Caesar's image. You bear God's. That settles whose you are.

luke.subject: Day 21: Watch and pray
luke.title: Watch and pray
luke.body:
Good morning.

Jesus talks about hard days ahead and says: stand up and lift up your heads, because your redemption is drawing near. Hope has a posture.

luke.subject: Day 22: The last supper
luke.title: The last supper
luke.body:
Good morning.

This is my body given for you. Then Gethsemane, the betrayal, and Peter's bitter weeping. He knows what it costs, and He goes anyway.

luke.subject: Day 23: Father, forgive them
luke.title: Father, forgive them
luke.body:
Good morning.

The crucifixion, and Luke alone records the thief: Jesus, remember me when you come into your kingdom. Today you will be with me in paradise. Grace to the last hour.

luke.subject: Day 24: Christmas Eve: hearts burning
luke.title: Christmas Eve: hearts burning
luke.body:
Good morning.

You finish Luke tonight, on the road to Emmaus, hearts burning as He opens the Scriptures. And tomorrow morning, the manger will not read like a children's story anymore. You know exactly who was born. Merry Christmas.

luke.subject: Day 25: Christmas: the Word became flesh
luke.title: Christmas: the Word became flesh
luke.body:
Good morning.

Merry Christmas. Today, John 1: the Word became flesh and made his dwelling among us. This is what the manger meant. One verse of it is worth the whole morning.

luke.subject: Day 26: He washed their feet
luke.title: He washed their feet
luke.body:
Good morning.

This week we sit in John's upper room. Jesus, knowing He came from God and was returning to God, picked up a towel. Love looks like that.

luke.subject: Day 27: Let not your hearts
luke.title: Let not your hearts
luke.body:
Good morning.

I go to prepare a place for you. I am the way and the truth and the life. Peace I leave with you. Read it slowly; it was said to frightened friends the night before the cross.

luke.subject: Day 28: The vine
luke.title: The vine
luke.body:
Good morning.

Remain in me. Apart from me you can do nothing. As the year ends, this is the one word worth carrying into the next: remain.

luke.subject: Day 29: He prayed for you
luke.title: He prayed for you
luke.body:
Good morning.

Jesus prays for those who will believe through the disciples' message. That is you, by name, prayed for by Jesus the night before He died.

luke.subject: Day 30: Finished and risen
luke.title: Finished and risen
luke.body:
Good morning.

The cross and the empty tomb, John's telling. It is finished, and then Mary hears her name. Both of those words are for you.

luke.subject: Day 31: Follow me
luke.title: Follow me
luke.body:
Good morning.

The year ends on a beach at breakfast, with Jesus restoring Peter and saying the words He started with: follow me. That is the whole invitation for the new year. Happy New Year, friend.

thanks-drip.subject: One week until Give Thanks
thanks-drip.body:
Good morning, {{name}}.

One week from today we open the Psalms together.

Every day for a month: one psalm, one short note, and three things you are thankful for. By the end your list will be ninety long, and you can read it at the table.

If you picked the full pace, you will read all 150 Psalms this month. Either way, pick the time of day you will do it and set an alarm. Five minutes is enough.

See you on day one.

Heather

thanks-drip.subject: Three days. Who should build a list with you?
thanks-drip.body:
Good morning, {{name}}.

Three days until Give Thanks begins.

Gratitude grows faster out loud. Is there someone who should build a thanksgiving list alongside you this month? A friend, your kids, your small group?

Text them the link:

heatherlynwilson.com/challenge-thanks

See you soon.

Heather

thanks-drip.subject: Tomorrow we open the Psalms
thanks-drip.body:
Good morning, {{name}}.

Tomorrow morning your first psalm arrives.

Here is the whole method: read the psalm, let it point you at something, and write down three things you are thankful for. Do not aim for profound. Aim for true. Ninety true things by Thanksgiving will preach better than any sermon.

See you in the morning.

Heather

gospels-drip.subject: One week until we open the Gospels
gospels-drip.body:
Good morning, {{name}}.

One week from today we start reading the Gospels.

Here is the road: Mark shows you what Jesus did. John tells you who He is. Matthew proves He is the promised King. And then Luke sits you down at the manger on Christmas Eve, when you know exactly who that baby is.

If you picked Luke instead, even simpler: one chapter a day, done by Christmas Eve.

Pick your reading time this week and set the alarm. See you on day one.

Heather

gospels-drip.subject: Three days. Bring someone to Bethlehem.
gospels-drip.body:
Good morning, {{name}}.

Three days until God With Us begins.

Is there someone who should read the Gospels with you this Christmas? Someone far from church who might say yes to just reading about Jesus? This is the easiest invitation of the year.

heatherlynwilson.com/challenge-gospels

See you soon.

Heather

gospels-drip.subject: Tomorrow: Mark, chapter one
gospels-drip.body:
Good morning, {{name}}.

Tomorrow morning we start with Mark, the fastest gospel, and his favorite word: immediately.

Do not worry about study notes or getting every detail. Just read and watch Him. The whole month is built on one question the disciples keep asking: who is this? By Christmas Eve, you will know the answer better than you ever have.

See you in the morning.

Heather

full-bible-v2.subject: Day 1: Here we go. Genesis.
full-bible-v2.body:
Good morning.

Today is the day. You signed up for this. I signed up for this. And right now, a group of us are opening to Genesis 1 together.

Yes, the whole book of Genesis today. Fifty chapters. I am not going to sugarcoat it. That is a lot. But here is what I want you to know. Genesis reads fast. It is all story. Creation, the flood, Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Joseph. You will get pulled in.

Do not worry about understanding every detail. Do not stop to study. Just read. Let the words wash over you. You are not writing a paper. You are meeting God in His Word.

If you cannot finish all 50 chapters today, that is okay. Read what you can. Mark where you stopped. Come back to it. The goal is not perfection. The goal is showing up.

I am reading alongside you today.

Heather

full-bible-v2.subject: Day 2: Slavery, plagues, and a God who shows up
full-bible-v2.body:
Good morning.

Yesterday was Genesis. Today is Exodus. And the tone shifts fast.

The people of God go from favor to slavery in the first chapter. And then God raises up Moses, a man who did not want the job, to lead them out.

Here is what stood out to me when I read this. God did not wait for Moses to be ready. He did not wait for the people to have it together. He showed up because He heard them crying. That was enough.

Today you will read about plagues and Passover and the Red Sea and the Ten Commandments and the building of the tabernacle. It is a full book. Take it one chapter at a time.

You are on Day 2. You showed up again. That matters.

Heather

full-bible-v2.subject: Day 3: The one nobody looks forward to
full-bible-v2.body:
Good morning.

Leviticus. I know.

This is the book people quit on. All the rules about sacrifices and skin diseases and what to eat and what not to eat. It feels like reading a manual for a world that does not exist anymore.

But here is what I want you to see today. Every single rule in this book exists because God wanted to be close to His people. He was not trying to make their lives harder. He was teaching them how to live near a holy God and survive it.

The whole book is God saying, I want to dwell among you. Here is how.

So push through it. Read it fast if you need to. But do not skip it. There is something in there for you today.

If you are still going after Leviticus, you can handle anything this month throws at you.

Heather

full-bible-v2.subject: Day 4: Wandering starts here
full-bible-v2.body:
Good morning.

Numbers starts with a census. Then it turns into the story of a people who could not stop complaining.

God had rescued them. Parted the sea. Fed them from the sky. And they still grumbled. They still wanted to go back to Egypt. They still doubted.

And honestly, I see myself in them more than I want to admit.

How many times has God shown up in my life and I still doubted the next thing? How many times has He provided and I still worried about tomorrow?

That is the gift of reading the whole Bible like this. You start to see yourself in the story. Not always in the heroes. Sometimes in the people who could not stop looking back.

Keep going. You are almost through the wilderness.

Heather

full-bible-v2.subject: Day 5: Moses says goodbye
full-bible-v2.body:
Good morning.

It is Sunday.

You have read four books of the Bible this week. And woven through all of them is this idea of rest. In Genesis, God stopped on the seventh day. Not because He was tired. Because He was done, and what He made was good. In Exodus, He told the Israelites not to gather manna on the seventh day. He gave them a double portion on Friday so they would not have to work. Then He put rest right in the middle of the Ten Commandments. Remember the Sabbath. Keep it holy. In Leviticus, the rest went even further. Not just a day but a whole year every seven years. The land needed to breathe too.

Rest is not a reward for finishing your work. It is built into the rhythm God designed from the beginning.

Today is Deuteronomy, and Moses is going to repeat the commandments again. Including the Sabbath. But this time he gives a different reason. In Exodus, God said rest because He rested at creation. In Deuteronomy, Moses says rest because you were slaves in Egypt, and slaves do not get to rest. Rest is what free people do.

You are free. Rest in that today.

Deuteronomy is Moses giving his final speech. He knows he is not going into the Promised Land. He knows his time is almost up. And he spends his last days reminding the people of everything God has done.

Remember. Do not forget. Tell your children. Remember.

He says it over and over. Because he knows what happens when people forget.

Pay attention to the heart behind this book. This is a man who walked with God for forty years, standing at the edge of something he will never see, and his last words are not about himself. They are about making sure the next generation does not lose what matters.

Five days in. Five books down.

Heather

full-bible-v2.subject: Day 6: They finally get there
full-bible-v2.body:
Good morning.

After forty years in the wilderness, they cross into the Promised Land. Joshua is in charge now. And the very first thing God says to him is be strong and courageous.

He does not say be smart. He does not say have a plan. He says be strong and do not be afraid.

Joshua is full of battles and victories and territory being claimed. It moves fast. And there is something satisfying about reading it after all that wandering in Numbers and Deuteronomy.

They made it. Not because they were perfect. Because God kept His promise.

You are almost a week in. Be strong and keep going.

Heather

full-bible-v2.subject: Day 7: A boy in the temple hears God's voice
full-bible-v2.body:
Good morning.

Today is one of my favorite books. First Samuel. A woman named Hannah prays for a son. God gives her Samuel. She gives him back to God. And then this little boy lying in the temple hears the voice of God and does not even know what it is.

That image has always stayed with me. God speaking to a child in the dark. And the child saying, speak Lord, your servant is listening.

Then you get Saul. Then David. The giant. The friendship with Jonathan. The jealousy. The running. The caves.

First Samuel has everything. It reads like a novel. Enjoy it today.

Heather

full-bible-v2.subject: Day 8: David at his best and worst
full-bible-v2.body:
Good morning.

Second Samuel is David's reign. And it is complicated.

This is the man after God's own heart. The one who danced before the Lord. The one who wrote half the Psalms. And this is also the man who saw Bathsheba and everything fell apart.

I think we want our Bible heroes to stay heroes. But they do not. David is proof that you can love God deeply and still make devastating choices.

The thing that sets David apart is not that he never sinned. It is that he always came back. He repented. He grieved. He did not pretend.

That is the lesson I take from today. Not that I will get it right every time. But that when I do not, I can still come back.

Heather

full-bible-v2.subject: Day 9: Everything falls apart
full-bible-v2.body:
Good morning.

Second Kings is hard. You are watching two kingdoms fall. Bad king after bad king. A few good ones scattered in. Prophets warning. Nobody listening.

And then Babylon comes. Jerusalem falls. The temple that Solomon built gets destroyed. The people are carried into exile.

It is heavy. But do not rush past the grief of it. This matters. Because the rest of the Bible, the prophets, the Psalms, even the New Testament, is all shaped by this moment. Everything changed when the temple fell.

Some days the reading is going to be hard. Today is one of those days. But you are still here. And that matters.

Heather

full-bible-v2.subject: Day 10: The same story, different angle
full-bible-v2.body:
Good morning.

First Chronicles covers a lot of the same ground as Samuel and Kings. You are going to recognize stories. You might wonder why it is here.

Here is what I want you to notice. Chronicles was written after the exile. The people had lost everything and come back. And someone sat down and retold their history, but this time with an emphasis on worship. On the temple. On what God had done.

When you lose everything and then look back, you see different things. You see the hand of God in places you missed the first time.

Yes, the genealogies at the beginning are long. Power through them. The rest of the book will reward you.

Almost two weeks in. You are doing this.

Heather

full-bible-v2.subject: Day 11: They go home
full-bible-v2.body:
Good morning. Two weeks in.

Today is three books. Ezra, Nehemiah, and Esther. They are shorter and they move fast.

Ezra is about rebuilding the temple. Nehemiah is about rebuilding the wall. Esther is about a woman who saved her people by showing up when it mattered most.

All three books are about restoration. About going back to the rubble and building something again. About courage in hard places.

If you are feeling the weight of this challenge right now, if two weeks in feels like a lot, these three books are for you today. Because they are proof that broken things get rebuilt. And it starts with one person who says I will go.

You are halfway to halfway. Keep going.

Heather

full-bible-v2.subject: Day 12: The hardest question in the Bible
full-bible-v2.body:
Good morning.

Job. The whole thing. Forty-two chapters.

A man who did everything right loses everything. His children. His health. His wealth. His friends show up and tell him he must have done something wrong. He insists he did not. And for most of the book, God is silent.

And then God speaks. And He does not answer the question. He does not explain why. He just says, I am God and you are not. Where were you when I laid the foundations of the earth?

That answer is not satisfying to our human brains. But it is the truth. We do not always get to know why. We just get to know who.

This book will wreck you if you let it. Let it.

You are almost halfway through the Bible.

Heather

full-bible-v2.subject: Day 13: God answers Job, and the songs begin
full-bible-v2.body:
Good morning.

Today you finish Job, and you get to the part everyone waits for. God finally speaks.

And here is what gets me every time. God never answers Job's question. He does not explain the suffering. Instead He asks Job about the ocean and the stars and the wild donkeys, and somehow that is enough. Job says, I had heard of you, but now my eyes have seen you.

Sometimes God does not give us answers. He gives us Himself. And it turns out that is what we actually needed.

Then, this very same day, you open the songbook. The Psalms. After twelve days of story and law and history, you get poetry. Real prayers from real people who were angry and afraid and grateful and amazed, sometimes all in the same chapter.

Do not rush the Psalms. Let a line stop you. When one does, that is not you falling behind. That is the whole point.

See you tomorrow.
Heather

full-bible-v2.subject: Day 14: Halfway. You made it to the Psalms.
full-bible-v2.body:
Good morning.

Sixteen days in. You are officially past the halfway mark of this challenge. And today you land in the Psalms.

The Psalms are different from everything you have read so far. This is not history. This is not law. This is people talking to God. Crying out. Praising. Asking why. Thanking Him. Begging for help. Declaring His faithfulness.

You are going to read fifty of them today. Some will hit you like a freight train. Some will feel repetitive. That is okay. The Psalms were never meant to be read in one sitting. But there is something about reading them in bulk that shows you the full range of what it looks like to walk with God.

Read them out loud if you can. Even a few. They were written to be spoken.

Halfway there. I am so proud of you.

Here is my one ask for the second half: tell someone.

Not so you have a buddy to keep you accountable. Tell them because of what this has been for you. If reading the Word this way has meant something, if it has shifted how you see God or how you read the Bible, there is someone in your life who needs that too. Good things are meant to be handed to other people.

You do not even have to find the words. Here is something you can copy, change to sound like you, and post or text to a friend:

"Reading the whole Bible in a month has changed how I read it. Not as individual verses and stories, but the big picture. I am halfway through. You can start any day you want. Come do it with me. heatherlynwilson.com/challenge #31DayBibleChallenge"

Post it, text it, drop it in your group chat. Someone else meeting God in His Word could start with your one sentence.

Heather

full-bible-v2.subject: Day 15: More Psalms. Stay with it.
full-bible-v2.body:
Good morning.

Fifty more Psalms today. And I want to point you to one in particular. Psalm 51.

This is David after Bathsheba. After the prophet Nathan confronted him. And David writes the most honest prayer of repentance in the entire Bible. Create in me a clean heart, O God.

That prayer has been prayed by millions of people over thousands of years. Because we have all been there. Maybe not David's sin. But the feeling of knowing you blew it and desperately needing God to make it right.

If you are behind on reading, this is your Psalm 51 moment. Do not quit. Just come back. Read today. That is enough.

Heather

full-bible-v2.subject: Day 16: The last of the Psalms
full-bible-v2.body:
Good morning.

Last fifty Psalms today. And they end with a crescendo.

Psalm 150. Let everything that has breath praise the Lord. That is how the book of Psalms closes. After all the crying, the questioning, the anger, the grief, the doubt, it ends with praise.

I think there is something in that for all of us. The journey does not end in the hard stuff. It ends in worship.

You just read the entire book of Psalms in three days. One hundred and fifty chapters. That is remarkable.

Eighteen days down. Thirteen to go.

Heather

full-bible-v2.subject: Day 17: Wisdom for the rest of your life
full-bible-v2.body:
Good morning.

Three books today. All wisdom literature. All different.

Proverbs is practical. Do this, not that. Fear the Lord, get wisdom, watch your mouth, work hard. You could read one chapter of Proverbs every day for a month and your life would change.

Ecclesiastes is the opposite. Solomon, the wisest man alive, looking at everything and saying it is all meaningless. It sounds depressing until you realize what he is actually saying. Without God, none of it matters. That is not despair. That is the most honest thing anyone has ever written.

Song of Solomon is a love poem. It is in the Bible and it is beautiful and it is supposed to be there.

Enjoy today. After the weight of Job and Psalms, this is a different kind of reading.

Heather

full-bible-v2.subject: Day 18: The prophet nobody wanted to listen to
full-bible-v2.body:
Good morning.

You are in the prophets now. And we start with Isaiah, the biggest of them all.

Isaiah is two things at once. It is God saying to His people, you have wandered so far and judgment is coming. And it is God saying, but I am not done with you. A savior is coming. Comfort my people.

Today is the first half. The harder half. Judgment. Warnings. Consequences. But even in the middle of it, you will find verses that stop you in your tracks. For unto us a child is born. That is Isaiah 9.

The prophets are harder to read than the stories. They are poetry and proclamation mixed together. Do not worry about understanding every verse. Just keep moving forward.

Twenty days. You are almost there.

Heather

full-bible-v2.subject: Day 19: Comfort, comfort my people
full-bible-v2.body:
Good morning. Three weeks in.

Today is the second half of Isaiah. And the tone changes. Starting around chapter 40, you hit some of the most beautiful passages in the Bible.

Comfort, comfort my people. Those who wait on the Lord shall renew their strength. He was wounded for our transgressions. By his stripes we are healed.

Isaiah wrote these words hundreds of years before Jesus. And when you read them now, knowing the rest of the story, it takes your breath away.

This might be your favorite day of reading this entire month. Let it soak in.

Three weeks done. Ten days left. You are going to finish this.

Heather

full-bible-v2.subject: Day 20: The prophet who did not want the job
full-bible-v2.body:
Good morning.

Jeremiah was called before he was born. And his first response was, I am too young. I do not know how to speak.

Sound familiar? Moses said the same thing. Gideon said the same thing. Every person God calls seems to start by explaining why they are the wrong choice.

Jeremiah spent his entire life preaching to people who would not listen. He wept over a nation that refused to turn back. He was thrown in prison. Dropped in a muddy cistern. And he kept going.

Sometimes faithfulness does not look like success. Sometimes it just looks like showing up to the thing God asked you to do, even when nobody is responding.

Nine days left. Keep showing up.

Heather

full-bible-v2.subject: Day 21: Jerusalem falls. Jeremiah weeps.
full-bible-v2.body:
Good morning.

Today you finish Jeremiah and read Lamentations. And it is heavy.

Jerusalem falls. The thing Jeremiah warned about for decades finally happens. And then Lamentations is his grief poured out on the page. Five chapters of mourning.

But right in the middle, chapter 3, you will find this. Great is His faithfulness. His mercies are new every morning.

That verse was not written on a good day. It was written in the ruins. And that is what makes it so powerful. It is not optimism. It is faith that survived the worst thing.

If you are tired today, if this challenge feels like a lot, read Lamentations 3:22-23. Mercy is new this morning. For you too.

Heather

full-bible-v2.subject: Day 22: Visions, bones, and a valley that comes alive
full-bible-v2.body:
Good morning.

Big day today. Ezekiel and Daniel.

Ezekiel is strange and beautiful. Wheels within wheels. A valley of dry bones that come back to life. A temple described in painstaking detail. This is a prophet who saw things no one else saw.

The valley of dry bones in chapter 37 is one of the most powerful images in all of Scripture. Can these bones live? And God says, watch me.

Daniel is the lion's den. The fiery furnace. Three young men who said, our God is able to deliver us, but even if He does not, we will not bow.

Even if He does not. That is the kind of faith I want.

One week left. Seven more days.

Heather

full-bible-v2.subject: Day 23: Twelve books in one day
full-bible-v2.reading: Hosea 5–14, Joel 1–3, Amos 1–9, Obadiah, Jonah 1–4, Micah 1–7, Nahum 1–3, Habakkuk 1–3
full-bible-v2.body:
Good morning.

Today is the minor prophets. All twelve of them. They are called minor because they are short, not because they are less important.

Hosea is about a prophet told to marry an unfaithful woman as a picture of God's love for Israel. Joel is about a plague of locusts and the day of the Lord. Amos is a shepherd who told the rich to stop exploiting the poor. Jonah ran from God and ended up in a fish.

Micah tells you what God requires. Do justice. Love mercy. Walk humbly.

Habakkuk asks God why bad things happen and gets an answer he did not expect.

Malachi is the last word of the Old Testament. And then silence. Four hundred years of silence before the New Testament begins.

You just finished the Old Testament. Let that sink in. Tomorrow you open to Matthew.

Heather

full-bible-v2.subject: Day 24: Jesus is here
full-bible-v2.body:
Good morning.

After everything you have read, all the promises and prophecies and waiting, today you open to the New Testament. And the very first word of Matthew connects Jesus to Abraham and David. The whole story has been leading here.

Two Gospels today. Matthew and Mark. Matthew is detailed and teaching-heavy. The Sermon on the Mount is in chapters 5 through 7 and it will change your life if you let it. Mark is fast. He uses the word immediately more than any other writer. Everything moves.

You have spent 25 days reading about a God who promised He would come. Today He arrives.

Six days left.

Heather

full-bible-v2.subject: Day 25: The cross, the empty tomb, and a manger
full-bible-v2.body:
Good morning.

Today is a big one. You will read the crucifixion and the resurrection in Matthew, then all of Mark, and then, of all things, you will end the day at the manger in Luke.

Strange order? Maybe. But think about what it does. You will watch Jesus die and rise, hear Mark tell the whole story again at full speed, and then see the baby in the feed trough and know exactly who He is and exactly what He came to do.

Mark is my favorite gospel to read fast. His favorite word is immediately. Jesus moves through Mark like a man on a mission, because He was.

By tonight you will have seen the whole gospel story twice and its beginning a third time. Let it stack up in you. This is the center of everything we believe.

See you tomorrow.
Heather

full-bible-v2.subject: Day 26: Two more portraits of Jesus
full-bible-v2.body:
Good morning.

Luke and John today. Two more Gospels. Same Jesus. Completely different angles.

Luke is the historian. He tells you about the shepherds, the prodigal son, the good Samaritan, Zacchaeus in the tree. He notices the people everyone else overlooks. The poor. The women. The outsiders.

John is the poet. In the beginning was the Word. I am the bread of life. I am the light of the world. I am the resurrection and the life. John is not trying to give you facts. He is trying to show you who Jesus really is.

You have now read all four Gospels. Four witnesses. One story. And you are four days from the finish line.

Heather

full-bible-v2.subject: Day 27: Believe, and then go
full-bible-v2.body:
Good morning.

Today you finish John and watch the church be born in Acts.

John wrote his gospel for one reason, and he tells you what it is near the end. These are written so that you may believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and that by believing you may have life in his name. Every sign, every conversation, every I AM statement is aimed at that one target. Your belief.

And then Acts. The same disciples who hid behind locked doors are suddenly standing in the streets preaching to thousands. What changed? They saw Him alive, and then the Holy Spirit showed up. The church does not grow in Acts because the plan was clever. It grows because God was in it.

That same Spirit is in you. That is not a nice thought. It is the actual claim of this book.

See you tomorrow.
Heather

full-bible-v2.subject: Day 28: The church explodes and Paul changes everything
full-bible-v2.body:
Good morning.

Acts is one of the most exciting books in the Bible. Jesus ascends. The Holy Spirit falls. Peter preaches and 3,000 people believe in a single day. And then a man named Saul, who was killing Christians, gets knocked off his horse and becomes Paul, the greatest missionary who ever lived.

The book of Acts reads like an action movie. Shipwrecks. Prison breaks. Miracles. Riots. And through all of it, the gospel spreads.

Then Romans. Paul's masterpiece. This is the deepest theology in the New Testament. For all have sinned. Nothing can separate us from the love of God. Take it slow if you can. Romans is dense but every sentence matters.

Three more days.

P.S. I do not want you to lose this momentum when you finish. Whenever you are ready for what is next, One Book Deep is open: the book of James every day for a month, going deep instead of fast. heatherlynwilson.com/challenge-james


Heather

full-bible-v2.subject: Day 29: Letters to churches that sound like they were written yesterday
full-bible-v2.reading: 1 Corinthians 8–16, 2 Corinthians 1–13, Galatians 1–6, Ephesians 1–6, Philippians 1–4, Colossians 1–2
full-bible-v2.body:
Good morning.

Paul's letters today. And they are surprisingly practical.

Corinthians is Paul writing to a messy church. Divisions. Lawsuits. Arguments about food. And right in the middle, chapter 13, the love chapter. Love is patient. Love is kind. You have heard it at weddings. But Paul did not write it for weddings. He wrote it for a church that was tearing itself apart.

Galatians is freedom. Ephesians is identity. Philippians is joy written from a prison cell. Colossians is who Jesus really is.

These letters are short. They read fast. And they will hit you differently after having read the whole Old Testament to get here. You understand now what they are building on.

Two more days.

P.S. Two days left. Start thinking about what comes next. One Book Deep is open, the book of James every day for a month: heatherlynwilson.com/challenge-james. Or see every challenge that is open at heatherlynwilson.com/challenge


Heather

full-bible-v2.subject: Day 30: One more day after this
full-bible-v2.reading: Colossians 3–4, 1 Thessalonians 1–5, 2 Thessalonians 1–3, 1 Timothy 1–6, 2 Timothy 1–4, Titus 1–3, Philemon, Hebrews 1–13, James 1–3
full-bible-v2.body:
Good morning.

Penultimate day. You are one day away from finishing.

Today is the rest of Paul's letters plus Hebrews. These are shorter books. Some are only a few chapters. But they are full.

Thessalonians is about the return of Jesus. Timothy and Titus are Paul coaching younger leaders. Philemon is a one-page letter about a runaway slave that will break your heart.

And then Hebrews. Nobody knows for sure who wrote it. But it ties the entire Old Testament to Jesus in a way that will make everything you have read this month click into place. Chapter 11 is the faith hall of fame. By faith Abraham. By faith Moses. By faith Rahab. These are your people now. You have read their stories.

One more day. You are going to finish this.

P.S. Tomorrow is your last day. It does not have to be the end. One Book Deep, the book of James every day for a month, is open whenever you are ready: heatherlynwilson.com/challenge-james


Heather

full-bible-v2.subject: Day 31: You did it.
full-bible-v2.reading: James 4–5, 1 Peter 1–5, 2 Peter 1–3, 1 John 1–5, 2 John, 3 John, Jude, Revelation 1–22
full-bible-v2.body:
Good morning.

This is it. Day 31. The last day.

James is practical faith. Do not just hear the word, do it. First Peter is hope in suffering. Second Peter is holding on. John's letters are about love. Jude is a warning. And then Revelation.

Revelation is wild and beautiful and confusing and hopeful all at once. Do not try to figure out every symbol. Just read it and let the ending wash over you. Because the Bible ends with a promise. He is making all things new. There will be no more tears. No more death. No more pain.

The story that started in a garden ends in a city. The story that started with God walking with two people ends with God dwelling among all His people forever.

You just read the entire Bible in 31 days.

I do not know what this month has done in your heart. But I know God's Word does not return empty. Something shifted. Something grew. Something was planted that will keep growing long after today.

I am so proud of you. Thank you for reading alongside me.

P.S. And I am not done. Each time you read the Word, God can show you new things about Himself and about yourself. Whenever you are ready for the next step: One Book Deep, the book of James every day for a month, at heatherlynwilson.com/challenge-james. Or see everything that is open at heatherlynwilson.com/challenge
